info.title: Terramantle API
info.summary: Private Terraform & OpenTofu registry, state backend, plan gate and provider supply chain.
info.description:
Terramantle is a private registry and governance plane for Terraform / OpenTofu. One Cloudflare
Worker serves every surface below, which is why they share one spec:

| Surface | Prefix | Spoken by |
|---|---|---|
| Service discovery | `/.well-known/` | `terraform` / `tofu`, the CLI, the portal SPA |
| Registry Protocol v1 — modules | `/v1/modules/` | `terraform` / `tofu` |
| Registry Protocol v1 — providers | `/v1/providers/` | `terraform` / `tofu` |
| State backend (HTTP) | `/state/{org}/` | the `http` state backend |
| Plan ingest | `/plans/{org}/` | CI, after `terraform show -json` |
| Management API | `/api/` | the portal SPA, the `terramantle` CLI, CI |
| Internal ingest | `/internal/`, `/api/internal/` | scanners, the Argo build fleet, OPA |

## Getting started

1. **Discover.** `GET /.well-known/terramantle-cli.json` returns the OIDC issuer, the audience
   every token must carry, and the public device-flow client id. Nothing else needs to be
   configured out of band. The portal's equivalent is
   `GET /.well-known/terramantle-portal.json`.
2. **Get a token.** Humans run authorization-code + PKCE against the portal application
   (`oidcPortal`); the CLI runs the device grant against its own application; CI either mints a
   machine `client_credentials` token or presents its native GitHub/GitLab OIDC token (see
   `vcsOidc`). Every token must carry the registry audience — request the `terramantle` scope
   or the Worker rejects the bearer on `aud`.
3. **Call the API.** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Terraform's `http` state backend cannot
   send a bearer, so the state and plan surfaces also accept HTTP Basic with the token in the
   password half (`basicAuth`).

## Conventions

- Collections are plural nouns; the HTTP method carries the verb. The few RPC-shaped
  exceptions are explicit state transitions on a resource (`.../rescan`, `.../promote`,
  `.../approve`) and are documented as such.
- Request and response bodies are `application/json` unless stated. Timestamps are
  **epoch milliseconds** (integer), matching the D1 columns behind them.
- Filtering, paging and sorting go in query parameters (`limit`, `offset`, …); identity goes
  in the path.
- Errors are a flat `{ "error": "<machine_code>", "message": "<human text>" }`
  (`#/components/schemas/Error`). The `error` code is the stable contract — match on it, not
  on `message`. Two surfaces deliberately differ: the Registry Protocol routes answer
  `{ "errors": [...] }` as HashiCorp's protocol requires
  (`#/components/schemas/RegistryErrors`), and a tier limit answers `402` with
  `#/components/schemas/QuotaExceeded`.

## Status codes used across the API

| Code | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| `200` / `201` / `204` | Success. `204` is also the Registry Protocol's module-download response, and "no state yet". |
| `202` | Accepted but not finished — a publish that was still scanning when the client's `wait` budget ran out. |
| `400` | Malformed request: bad JSON, a missing required field, an unparseable version constraint. |
| `401` | No credential, or one that failed validation. |
| `402` | A plan/tier limit was hit. Not a failure — see `QuotaExceeded`. |
| `403` | Authenticated but not allowed: wrong role, not a member, a bot on a human-only action, a blocked artefact. |
| `404` | Not found, or a feature kill-switch is off, or an artefact deliberately hidden (`serve_mode: block`). |
| `405` | Right path, wrong method on the protocol routers. |
| `409` | Conflict: a concurrent claim, or a duplicate. |
| `410` | Endpoint removed. The body names its replacement. |
| `413` | Body over the surface's cap (100 MB state/plan, 10 MB lock file). |
| `422` | Well-formed but semantically rejected (unknown tier, unsupported upstream, unresolvable source repo). |
| `423` | Locked: the policy gate blocked this workspace's next apply. |
| `429` | Rate limited (the policy-settings debounce). |
| `500` | Unhandled. |
| `502` | A dependency the Worker fronts failed (upstream registry, queue send). |
| `503` | Feature not enabled, or a required binding/credential is unconfigured. |

## Companions

- **Queue contracts.** The asynchronous half of the platform — every Cloudflare Queue message
  between the Worker, the scanners and the Argo build fleet — is specified in AsyncAPI 3.0 at
  `packages/queue-contracts/asyncapi.yaml`, served from `GET /asyncapi.json`.
- **Policy input.** The JSON Schema for the OPA policy `input` document is served live from
  `GET /api/policy-schema` — it is generated from the Worker's own types, so it is the
  authority for policy authors rather than anything restated here.

servers.description: Production. Serves every surface in this spec.

Org-scoped provider registry. `GET /.well-known/terraform.json` on this host advertises
`providers.v1: /v1/providers/{orgSlug}/`, so `tofu` appends provider sources to the
org-scoped route. The subdomain is a ROUTING hint only and never authenticates anything —
membership is still enforced per request. Only the Registry Protocol is served here; the
`/api/*` management layer stays on the bare host.

audience and its own client id, so none of it is baked into a binary or a bundle.

bearerAuth.description:
An OIDC access token in `Authorization: Bearer`. Three kinds validate here, and the Worker
routes validation by the token's `iss`:

- **Human** — authorization-code + PKCE against the portal application. Carries `email`,
  so RBAC resolves org membership from it.
- **Machine** — `client_credentials` against a confidential application (CI, scanners,
  automation). No `email`, so it is treated as a bot: capped at `member`, and refused
  outright on human-only actions.
- **VCS** — a native GitHub Actions / GitLab CI token, resolved against the org's VCS trust
  entries instead of a client registration (see `vcsOidc`).

Every token must carry the registry audience; request the `terramantle` scope to get it.

basicAuth.description:
HTTP Basic, where the **password half carries the token** and the username is ignored.
Terraform's `http` state backend has no bearer option, so the state and plan surfaces
accept the same credentials this way. Equivalent to `bearerAuth` in every other respect.

oidcPortal.description:
The human portal's OIDC application. `GET /.well-known/terramantle-portal.json` returns
this URL for the deployment being called, which is the value to trust — the literal above
is the production default and is rewritten on the spec served from `GET /openapi.json`.

oauth2Portal.description:
The same portal application expressed as an OAuth2 authorization-code + PKCE flow, so the
interactive docs at `GET /docs` can obtain a real token and call the API as the signed-in
human. The client is public and holds no secret; PKCE is mandatory. Its redirect URI
(`{origin}/docs/oauth2-redirect`) is registered on the application in the IdP.

scopes.email: Email — what RBAC resolves org membership from.
scopes.terramantle: Stamps the registry `aud` and the `roles` claim. Without it the Worker rejects the token.

vcsOidc.description:
A GitHub Actions or GitLab CI OIDC token, presented as a bearer (or in the Basic password
half). No client registration: the Worker validates the token against the issuer, checks
`aud` equals the configured VCS audience, then matches `sub` against the org's VCS trust
entries (`/api/orgs/{orgId}/vcs-trust`). The matched entry decides the org.

A `sub` trusted by more than one org resolves to the **most specific** matching pattern;
anything ambiguous fails closed with `401`. These identities are bots: capped at `member`
and refused on human-only actions.

archiveSignature.name: sig
archiveSignature.description:
An HMAC capability URL, not a credential the caller holds. `terraform`/`tofu` do not
forward `Authorization` when following a download URL, so the Worker mints short-lived
signed URLs for archives and provider files. Entitlement was checked when the URL was
minted; the serve path re-checks blocks and yanks before returning bytes, so a URL minted
before a block does not still resolve to data.

scannerSecret.description:
**Internal.** Either the scanner's OIDC service identity (the only accepted `azp` is the
configured scanner client) or, as a fallback during the OIDC migration, the static
`SCANNER_SECRET` bearer. Fails closed when the scanner client id is unconfigured.

argoResultsSecret.description:
**Internal.** The `ARGO_RESULTS_SECRET` bearer presented by the in-cluster Argo build
Workflow and the queue supervisor. These routes also accept `scannerSecret`.

opaGateOidc.description:
**Internal.** An Authentik `client_credentials` token carrying the `opa-gate` scope, minted
by the OPA gate service. Scope-based rather than role-based on purpose: this is the only
caller that reads every tenant's policy bundle.

webhookSecret.name: X-Webhook-Secret
webhookSecret.description: Shared secret for R2 event notifications, compared in constant time.

stripeSignature.name: Stripe-Signature
stripeSignature.description: Stripe's webhook signature, verified in the handler. No other auth applies.

OrgId.name: orgId
OrgId.description: Org UUID **or** slug. Both are accepted everywhere `orgId` appears.

Workspace.name: workspace
Workspace.description:
State workspace name — a single path segment on the management API. Workspaces whose key
contains slashes on the protocol router appear here with those slashes percent-encoded.

Namespace.name: namespace
Namespace.description:
For modules, the owning org's slug. For providers, the upstream provider namespace
(e.g. `hashicorp`).

Upstream.name: upstream
Upstream.description:
Which lineage of this provider the org manages. An org can manage the same
`namespace/type` from both registries independently; the client's `User-Agent` picks
between them when serving.

ProviderVersion.name: version
ProviderVersion.description:
Provider version. A self-built artifact is always a revision of an upstream base,
`<base>-0.0.<rev>` (e.g. `6.3.3-0.0.2`).

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Clamped to the endpoint's documented maximum.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Caller-generated key that makes this mutation replay-safe. Required: a retry of a state
mutation must not apply twice. A repeat with the same key returns the first outcome with
`idempotent_replay: true`.

ScanVersionId.name: versionId
ScanVersionId.description: Version row id. Resolved across every tenant — see this file's auth note.

UserId.name: userId
UserId.description: `users.id` — the internal UUID, not the OIDC subject.

RemovedPath.name: path
RemovedPath.description: Any sub-path. Matched as a wildcard; every method answers `410`.

ModuleNamespace.name: namespace
ModuleNamespace.description: Owning org's slug. For modules the namespace **is** the org.

ModuleProvider.name: provider
ModuleProvider.description:
Target provider, per the registry protocol's `namespace/name/provider` triple. Part of the
module's identity, not a reference to a provider artefact.

ProviderOrgSlug.name: orgSlug
ProviderOrgSlug.description:
Org slug whose registry answers. Membership is enforced per request — the slug is never
itself an authorization.

ProviderOs.name: os
ProviderOs.description: Target OS, as Terraform names it.

ProviderArch.name: arch
ProviderArch.description: Target architecture, as Terraform names it.

ProviderFileUpstream.name: upstream
ProviderFileUpstream.description:
Mirrored lineage this file belongs to. The `self_built` sentinel is invalid here — use the
`self_built/{lineage}` path family, which carries the lineage segment the object key needs.

ProviderLineage.name: lineage
ProviderLineage.description:
For a self-built artifact, the registry its source tree came from. Part of the object key:
the same provider built from both registries produces two independent artifacts.

ProviderFilename.name: filename
ProviderFilename.description: Zip filename exactly as named in `SHA256SUMS`.

ArchiveSig.name: sig
ArchiveSig.description:
HMAC signature from the download document. Present ⇒ the signature is the authorization and
no `Authorization` header is read. Absent ⇒ a token is required.

StateKey.name: key
StateKey.description:
Workspace key. The protocol router matches a **wildcard**, so this may contain slashes
(`prod/backend`) — which OpenAPI path templating cannot express. Treat the template as
"the rest of the path".

BadRequest.description: Malformed request — bad JSON, a missing required field, or an unparseable value.

example.message: `action` must be "block", "allow" or null

Unauthorized.description: No credential was presented, or the one presented failed validation.

Forbidden.description:
Authenticated, but not allowed: insufficient role, not a member of this org, a machine
token on a human-only action, or a blocked artefact.

value.message: This action must be performed by a human user

NotFound.description:
No such resource. Also returned when a feature kill-switch is off, and when an artefact is
deliberately hidden rather than refused (`serve_mode: block`).

example.message: Workspace not found

Conflict.description: The request lost a race, or duplicates something that already exists.

example.message: A concurrent build claimed this revision; please retry
Invalid tier

QuotaExceeded.description:
A tier limit was reached. This is an expected business outcome rather than a failure: the
body names the limit, what was counted, and the tier that would raise it.

example.message: State file exceeds 100MB limit

Gone.description: This endpoint was removed. The body names its replacement.

example.message: This endpoint was removed. Provider serving, builds and governance live under /api/orgs/:orgId/providers.

InternalError.description: Unhandled server error. The `req_id` in the Worker log correlates to the trace.

example.message: An unexpected error occurred

NotEnabled.description:
The feature is disabled by a deploy-time switch, or a binding/credential it needs is
unconfigured.

example.message: Self-built providers are not enabled

UpstreamFailed.description: A dependency the Worker fronts failed — the upstream registry, or a queue send.

example.message: Scan could not be queued; please retry

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
The platform's error body. `error` is a stable machine code — branch on it. `message` is
for humans and may change at any time.

allOf.description: An `Error` that also names the fields at fault.

missing.description: Fields that were required and absent or unusable.

RegistryErrors.title: RegistryErrors
RegistryErrors.description:
The Terraform Registry Protocol's error envelope. Used **only** on `/v1/*` routes, because
`terraform`/`tofu` surface `detail` to the operator verbatim — which is how a policy block
explains itself at the point of failure.

errors.title: Module blocked by policy
errors.detail: This module version is not consumable. Failed policies: no-public-ingress

QuotaExceeded.title: QuotaExceeded
QuotaExceeded.description:
Returned with `402`. A tier limit is a business outcome, not an application error — it is
recorded as such in telemetry and never pages anyone.

current.description: Count at the time of the refusal.

max.description: Ceiling on the org's current tier.

upgrade_tier.description: Lowest tier that would allow the request.

Ok.title: Ok
Ok.description: Minimal acknowledgement for an action with nothing to return.

Role.title: Role
Role.description:
Org role, ranked `reader` < `member` < `admin` < `owner`. A guard states a minimum, so a
higher role always passes. Machine identities never exceed `member` whatever this says.

Tier.title: Tier
Tier.description: Billing tier. Drives every quota in `QuotaExceeded`.

UpstreamRegistry.title: UpstreamRegistry
UpstreamRegistry.description:
A public provider registry Terramantle mirrors from. The client's `User-Agent` decides
which lineage an org serves when it manages both (`OpenTofu/` ⇒ `opentofu.org`).

ProviderUpstream.title: ProviderUpstream
ProviderUpstream.description:
`UpstreamRegistry`, plus the `self_built` sentinel for artifacts Terramantle compiled and
signed itself. A self-built row also records the registry lineage its source came from.

ServeMode.title: ServeMode
ServeMode.description:
Whether an org's registry answers for this provider.

- `off` — managed and scanned, but not served. `403` on the version list.
- `serve` — served, subject to the policy gate and per-version blocks.
- `block` — hidden. The version list `404`s so the provider does not advertise that it
  exists at all.

ServeOverride.title: ServeOverride

PolicyArtefactType.title: PolicyArtefactType
PolicyArtefactType.description: The artefact kinds a policy can be written against.

ActorType.title: ActorType
ActorType.description:
How the acting identity authenticated. Display and audit only — never an input to an
authorization decision.

Timestamp.title: Timestamp
Timestamp.description: Epoch milliseconds, matching the D1 column behind it.

modules.v1.description: Base path of the module registry protocol.

providers.v1.description:
Base path of the provider registry protocol. Org-scoped on an org subdomain, bare
otherwise.

ApiSpecLinks.title: ApiSpecLinks
ApiSpecLinks.description:
Where this deployment's machine-readable contract lives. Advertised for the same reason the
issuer is: a client should never have to be told, and the served documents have this
deployment's origin and issuer substituted in, which a committed copy cannot.

docs_redirect_uri.description:
The redirect URI `/docs` runs its PKCE flow against. Published so an operator can diff
it against the application's registered redirect URIs instead of guessing why sign-in
fails — a missing entry there is that flow's one failure mode.

api_url.description: Origin this document was served from — what the CLI should call.

issuer.description: Per-application OIDC issuer for the CLI's own client.

discovery_url.description: RFC 8414 metadata URL; the CLI resolves the device + token endpoints from it.

audience.description: Registry audience every user/CI token must carry.

vcs_audience.description:
Audience GitHub/GitLab CI must mint its OIDC token for. Falls back to `audience`
when no distinct VCS audience is configured.

device_client_id.description:
Public client for the device-authorization flow, or `null` until provisioned — in
which case the CLI reports a clear error rather than attempting a login.

scopes.description:
Space-separated scopes to request. `terramantle` is load-bearing: it stamps the
registry `aud` and the `roles` claim, and without it the Worker rejects the bearer.

client_id.description: Public PKCE client id, or `null` until provisioned.

FindingCategory.description:
Tool-agnostic finding category. The underlying scanner tool that produced
the finding is internal-only and is never surfaced in public API responses.

PublicModuleFinding.description: A finding attached to a module version, as returned by the registry API. The `tool` property is stripped at the API boundary and never exposed publicly.

rule_id.description: Scanner rule or check identifier, if available.

file_path.description: Path of the file in which the finding was detected, relative to the module root.

line_start.description: First line of the affected range (1-indexed).

line_end.description: Last line of the affected range (1-indexed, inclusive).

resource.description: Terraform resource address or identifier related to the finding.

meta.description: Free-form tool-specific metadata. Shape varies by category and rule.

PublicStateFinding.description: A finding derived from a Terraform state file, as returned by the GET /api/v1/{orgId}/state/{workspace}/findings endpoint. The `tool` property is stripped at the API boundary. There are no file_path or line_start/line_end fields (state files carry no source location).

rule_id.description: Scanner rule or check identifier, if available.

resource.description: Terraform resource address or identifier related to the finding.

meta.description:
Free-form metadata. For exposure findings, meta carries a `subtype`
discriminator string with one of the following values:
  - 'endpoint' — an exposed HTTP/HTTPS endpoint
  - 'port'     — an exposed network port

All other fields in meta are tool-specific and should not be relied
upon as stable contract.

InternalModuleFindingInput.description: A finding item within the scanner -> worker POST /internal/scan-results payload. Extends PublicModuleFinding with a required `tool` field and an optional `category` (the worker derives category from tool+rule_id when absent, during rollout).

tool.description: The scanner tool that produced this finding.

category.description:
Tool-agnostic category. Optional during rollout — the worker will
derive it from the tool and rule_id if absent. Once all scanners
populate this field it will become required.

InternalStateFindingInput.description: A finding item within the scanner -> worker POST /internal/scan-results/state payload. Extends PublicStateFinding with a required `tool` field and an optional `category` (same rollout semantics as InternalModuleFindingInput).

tool.description: The scanner tool that produced this finding.

category.description:
Tool-agnostic category. Optional during rollout — the worker derives
it from the tool and rule_id if absent.

meta.description:
Free-form metadata. For exposure findings, meta carries a `subtype`
discriminator string ('endpoint' | 'port').

PresignedUrl.title: PresignedUrl
PresignedUrl.description:
A short-lived presigned object-storage URL. The scan pod is untrusted and holds no bucket
credentials — this URL is the entire grant.

key.description: The object key the URL addresses.

ScanClaimResult.title: ScanClaimResult
ScanClaimResult.description:
Read both booleans. `claimed: false, proceed: true` is the interesting case: a previous
attempt may have died mid-run, and re-scanning is safe because ingest is a race-safe
upsert.

status.description: The job's current status, when the claim did not succeed.

ScanPolicyResultInput.title: ScanPolicyResultInput
ScanPolicyResultInput.description: One OPA verdict as a scanner reports it.

ModuleDependencyInput.title: ModuleDependencyInput
ModuleDependencyInput.description: One module-to-module dependency edge parsed from the source.

is_terramantle.description: Whether the dependency resolves inside this registry.

RequiredProviderRef.title: RequiredProviderRef
RequiredProviderRef.description:
One `required_providers` entry parsed from a module's source. This is how a provider becomes
a **discovered** artefact in the consuming org's catalog.

version_constraint.description: The constraint as written, or `null` when the source omitted one.

status.description: `failed` means the SCAN failed — distinct from a policy block.

required_providers.description: Drives provider discovery. Additive — an older scanner omits it.

StateScanResultsBody.title: StateScanResultsBody
StateScanResultsBody.description: Findings must carry metadata only — never a secret value.

policy_results.description:
A failing **enforcing** verdict sets the workspace block that the next apply's `LOCK` is
refused on. Stored whether or not policies are enabled, so re-enabling re-blocks.

real_resource_count.description:
Best-effort. Absent (older scanner) or `null` (classifier bailout) leaves the stored
columns untouched — which is also how pre-classification versions get backfilled.

category.description: Derived by the Worker from `tool` and `rule_id` when absent.

ProviderScanResultsBody.title: ProviderScanResultsBody
ProviderScanResultsBody.description:
One per scanned version. A job emits several; they attach to the job by `job_id`, which is
what makes the attachment race-safe when two jobs for one provider overlap.

org_id.description: `null` on a platform-scoped scan — an auto-patch patched-tree scan has no requesting org.

provider_type.description: Named `provider_type` rather than `type` to avoid the JavaScript collision.

job_failed.description:
A job-level terminal failure — for example a constraint that matched no versions. Marks
the whole job failed; the per-version fields are absent.

error_message.description: Job-level reason, or this version's reason on a `failed`/`skipped` report.

matched_count.description: Versions matching the constraint before the per-job cap. Constant across a job's reports.

status.description:
`published` ⇒ scanned. `failed` ⇒ attempted and failed (enters the retry tier).
`skipped` ⇒ **never attempted** because the job ran out of wall budget: no result row is
written and the backlog marker is re-armed for the next drain.

source_commit_sha.description: Exact upstream commit the version tag pointed at when scanned — source provenance.

scan_started_at.description: Scan start, epoch milliseconds. Duration is `scanned_at - scan_started_at`.

source_signals.description: Supply-chain trust signals from the source repository. Self-built only.

policy_results.description:
Self-built only. Materialised per-org, with the blocked gate derived from each policy's
enforcing flag.

BuildPlatformResult.title: BuildPlatformResult
BuildPlatformResult.description:
One platform the build produced. A platform that failed to compile is **excluded** rather
than reported as failed — publish-what-built.

PatchProvenanceInput.title: PatchProvenanceInput
PatchProvenanceInput.description:
On success, the git provenance of a patched build. On a failure report, the stage and
reason instead — which is what the UI and the auto-patch scheduler read to decide whether
to retry.

source_tree_hash.description:
Structural digest of the pinned source tree. The gate verdicts bind to this value —
it is what makes "the bytes scanned are the bytes built" checkable.

status.description: Present only from the failure reporter; absent means a successful publish.

attempt.description:
Which queue DELIVERY this workflow ran for (`0` = first). **The retry discriminator**: a
higher attempt than the stored row's re-opens a terminal row; equal-or-lower is a
duplicate and is ignored.

source_upstream.description:
The registry lineage the artifacts were published under. **Required on success** and
must equal the job row's lineage — it is part of the object key, so a mismatch is
refused rather than published somewhere nothing will look.

attempt.description: Retry attempt; `0` for the first run.

message.description: Node failure message, capped by the producer.

msg_key.description: The claim key — a build/scan job id, or a version id for module/state/plan scans.

workflow_name.description: `null` while the claim exists but no workflow has been observed yet.

phase.description: `null` when no workflow exists for the claim.

message.description: Workflow status message. Gate markers land here.

attempt.description: Queue delivery attempt of the lease this claim holds.

observed_at.description:
Supervisor clock when this state was observed. **The ordering guard** — the Worker drops
an event older than the stored timestamp, so a slow tick cannot overwrite newer state.

patch_failure.description: Structured patch failure, read from the patch node's output parameter.

settle.description: Present only on the tick that settled the queue message.

heartbeat.description:
Sent **every tick, even with zero claims**. Its absence is how the reapers tell a lost
workflow from a supervisor that is down.

at_capacity.description:
The pull loop is paused at its claim ceiling, so an unleased message may be
legitimate queued work — absence-based reaping must pause too.

list_ok.description:
`false` ⇒ this tick's cluster list failed. Claims cannot settle, but the lease side
is still alive, which is what the lost-message arm cares about.

BacklogProviderRef.title: BacklogProviderRef
BacklogProviderRef.description: How operator tooling names a provider version. The owning org is resolved server-side.

version.description: For a build, the upstream base (`X.Y.Z`) — never a revision.

id.description:
The internal user id. This, not the OIDC subject, is the identity other endpoints take
as `userId`.

slug.description:
URL-safe identity. Accepted anywhere `orgId` appears, and it is the `namespace` segment
for this org's modules.

claimed_domain.description: Email domain whose new sign-ups join this org automatically.

is_personal.description: A personal org is the user's own account. Always reports `starter`.

is_billing_admin.description: Grants billing access without promoting the member to `admin`.

last_seen_at.description:
Last authenticated request by this user, anywhere on the platform — not a login
event. The auth middleware writes it at most once per five minutes per identity
(same throttle as `MachineTokenSummary.last_used_at`), so read it as "recently
seen", and note that a still-valid session or a CLI call counts as activity
without anyone signing in again.

`null` means never seen — for an invited member that means they have not been
back since the login that created their user record, because
`POST /api/orgs/{orgId}/members` can only invite someone who has logged in at
least once.

Informational only: it exists so an owner can tell a live seat from a dormant
one. No authorization decision reads it, and it is not scoped to this org.

NotificationCadence.title: NotificationCadence
NotificationCadence.description: How often the org wants provider-update notifications.

subject.description: Pattern matched against the CI token's `sub`.

TokenScope.title: TokenScope
TokenScope.description:
What a machine token can reach.

- `global` — every org its creator administers.
- `org` — one org, with per-domain read/write via `include_modules` / `include_state`.
- `state_workspaces` — one org, but state only on the workspaces in `state_grants`.

StateTokenGrant.title: StateTokenGrant
StateTokenGrant.description: One workspace a `state_workspaces`-scoped token may touch, and how.

state_grants.description: Required in substance for `state_workspaces` scope — without grants the token reaches no state.

examples.name: prod-apply
examples.description: GitHub Actions apply job for prod

MachineTokenSummary.title: MachineTokenSummary
MachineTokenSummary.description:
A machine identity's metadata. Never carries a secret.

`last_used_at` and the geo fields are written at most once per five minutes per identity —
the auth middleware runs on every request and rewriting the row each time would churn it
for data nobody needs at sub-minute resolution. Read them as "recently seen".

oidc_client_id.description: The token's `azp`. This is the identity the API authorizes.

client_secret.description:
**Returned once, here.** Never stored and never retrievable again — a lost secret
means rotating the token.

TierFeatureFlags.title: TierFeatureFlags
TierFeatureFlags.description:
What the org's tier allows. A `false` flag is why an otherwise-valid request answers `402`
with `QuotaExceeded`.

providerServe.description: Whether the org's registry may answer provider requests at all.

usage.description: Current counts against the counted limits.

active.description: Whether the window is still open.

grace_period.description: `null` when no downgrade grace period is set.

has_stripe.description: Whether a Stripe subscription backs this org.

AuditAction.title: AuditAction
AuditAction.description: The governance actions recorded in the audit log.

actor_user_id.description: `null` for a platform-initiated action with no human actor.

metadata.description:
A **JSON string**, not an object — stored verbatim as written. Shape varies by
`action`; parse it per action rather than treating it as a stable contract.

DailyPoint.title: DailyPoint
DailyPoint.description: One UTC day. Series are sparse — days with no activity are omitted.

TenantAnalytics.title: TenantAnalytics
TenantAnalytics.description:
The org dashboard's payload. Rollup counts and series only — no resource values and no
state or plan contents.

Every series is **sparse**: days with no activity are omitted and the client zero-fills.
Totals and 30-day counts cover downloads; the per-module and per-workspace series cover 90
days.

top_module_download_series.description: Top 5 modules by downloads over 90 days, each with its daily series.

top_workspace_push_series.description: Top 5 workspaces by pushes over 90 days, each with its daily series.

patch_adoption.description: Continuous-patching exposure: vulnerable superseded versions still being downloaded.

module_findings_artifacts.description: Per-severity drill-down for the open-findings donuts.

version_count.description: `0` on a stub node for a dependency outside the caller's visibility.

is_terramantle.description: Whether the dependency resolves inside this registry.

PlanVersionSummary.description: Client-facing plan version summary (list + detail). Action counts derive from `resource_changes[].change.actions`; a replace (delete+create) counts ONCE under `replace_count`, not under add/destroy. No workspace_id / storage internals leak.

sensitive_change_count.description: Changes touching a sensitive attribute (count only, never the value).

attestation_hash.description: sha-256 of the redacted canonical plan JSON.

prior_serial.description: Prior state serial the plan was made against (from X-Plan-Prior-Serial).

PublicPlanFinding.description: A redacted finding attached to a plan version. The `tool` property is stripped at the API boundary (kept internal, mirrors PublicStateFinding). Plan findings carry an `attr` (the attribute that forces a replacement / carries the finding). No concrete value appears in any field.

description.description: Attribute path / metadata — never a concrete value.

attr.description: The attribute that forces replacement / carries the finding.

meta.description: Free-form metadata (e.g. `meta.provider` for a replacement). Value-free.

PlanPolicyResult.description: One persisted plan policy-evaluation result. `source` discriminates the synchronous built-in M2 gate (`builtin`, policy_id null) from the async advisory OPA pass (`opa`). Redacted-safe: `failure_msg` carries gate reasons only.

policy_id.description: Null for the built-in gate (no policies row).

failure_msg.description: Joined gate reasons when not passed; null when passed.

PlanAttestation.description: Apply-matches-review verdict for a (workspace, attestation_hash). `attested` = a plan_version with this hash was ingested/redacted here; `approved` = an active override binds a human review to this hash; `stale` = the plan's prior_serial trails the workspace's current state serial. FAIL-CLOSED: a CI gate MUST require `attested && approved && !stale`.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of the verdict (states the fail-closed rule).

ReplacementByProvider.description: Cross-workspace forced-replacement rollup for one provider (M5). `workspaces` is where this provider forces a delete+create in a recent plan; `blast_radius_ workspace_count` is how many workspaces use the provider at all.

provider.description: Provider label (meta.provider, else resource type prefix, else "unknown").

GateConfig.description: The built-in M2 gate configuration for a scope (org default when workspace-less; a per-workspace override otherwise — per-workspace wins). `destroy_denylist` is a JSON array of resource types. No config at all = an all-clear gate (never blocks).

max_destroys.description: Block if the plan's destroy count (incl. replace-halves) exceeds this. Null = no cap.

destroy_denylist.description: Block if any destroyed resource type is in this list (incl. replace-halves).

require_approval.description: Hold every plan pending manual approval when true.

PlanScanResultsBody.description: The plan-scanner -> worker POST /internal/scan-results/plan payload. Findings are metadata-only. `policy_results` are ADVISORY OPA verdicts (stored source='opa'); the enforcing built-in gate row is written inline at ingest and is never erased by a rescan.

PlanFindingInput.description: A finding item in the plan scan-results payload. Metadata only — `description`, `resource`, and `attr` are addresses/paths, NEVER a concrete value.

tool.description: Scanner tool that produced the finding (kept internal; not surfaced publicly).

category.description: Plan category (drift / replacement / secret_exposure / stateful_destroy). Free text.

PlanPolicyResultInput.description: An advisory OPA policy verdict in the plan scan-results payload. Upserted on UNIQUE(plan_version_id, policy_id) with source='opa'; never collides with the built-in (policy_id null) row.

OnMissingSignal.title: OnMissingSignal
OnMissingSignal.description:
How a **missing** trust signal is treated — not a failing one.

Named `signal_fail_gate` before policy-input contract v2; the old spelling is still
ACCEPTED on `PATCH` and still returned on `GET` for one release, because this endpoint is a
documented contract and callers do not deploy alongside the worker. The values are
unchanged.

- `ignore` — fail open. An artefact with no signal is allowed.
- `hard_fail` — fail closed. No signal is treated as a failure.

The highest-consequence field in the policy settings.

PolicyEnablement.title: PolicyEnablement
PolicyEnablement.description:
Which artefact kinds this org evaluates policies for. **Enforcement needs `opaTier` as well
as the toggle** — a toggle on with the tier gate off evaluates and reports but refuses
nothing.

global.description: Master switch. Off ⇒ nothing is enforced for any artefact kind.

opaTier.description:
Whether the org's tier includes custom policies. Read-only here — it comes from
billing, not from this endpoint.

signal_fail_gate.description: Former name of `on_missing_signal`. Returned for one release; do not read it.

allOf.title: PolicySettings
allOf.description: Enablement plus the current blast radius and who last changed it.

modules_blocked_count.description: Module versions currently blocked by an enforcing policy.

last_changed_by.description: Email of whoever last changed these settings, from the audit log.

changed.description:
`false` ⇒ the request changed nothing: no recompute, no rescan, no audit entry,
and the rate limit was not consumed.

rows_changed.description: Artefact rows whose consumability the recompute altered.

rego.description: The policy body. Always declares `package terramantle.policy`.

is_enforcing.description: `1` ⇒ a failing verdict blocks. `0` ⇒ it is recorded and reported only.

instance_key.description:
`null` ⇒ an org baseline, applying to every artefact of this kind and inheritable.
Set ⇒ identity-custom, attached to exactly one artefact identity.

eval_failing.description:
Evaluated versions that fail this policy. Present on an artefact-scoped list read;
absent on an unscoped one.

eval_failing_names.description: Comma-joined distinct names of the non-compliant artefacts, for a hover list.

PolicyMutationResult.title: PolicyMutationResult
PolicyMutationResult.description:
The policy after the change, plus the re-evaluation that change required. Changing a policy
makes existing verdicts stale, so the work is queued here rather than left to a cron — and
reported, so a caller is never left guessing whether the edit applied retroactively.

rescan.description: What was enqueued for re-evaluation. Coalesced per org.

BuildGate.title: BuildGate
BuildGate.description:
The gates a self-built provider must clear before it is signed. `G2_HIGH` is the
high-severity tier of `G2`, overridable separately from the rest.

VcsStats.title: VcsStats
VcsStats.description:
Cached repository-health signals for the provider's source repository. Always served from
cache — never a live fetch on a read path. `null` on the parent field means no resolvable
repository, or a cache row the scheduled refresh has not filled yet.

ProviderArtefactSummary.title: ProviderArtefactSummary
ProviderArtefactSummary.description:
One managed provider in the catalog list. Enrichment fields are fault-isolated: a failing
enrichment query reads as `0` or `null` for the affected rows rather than failing the list,
so a zero here is not proof of absence.

discovered.description: Created by a lock-file or module scan rather than added by hand.

source_url.description:
Effective source repository: the global row for this registry and provider, else the
per-org lock-file hint.

usage_workspace_count.description: Workspaces whose lock file pins this provider — its blast radius.

outdated.description:
At least one workspace locks a version behind its `latest_matching`. `false` also when
the usage enrichment was unavailable.

referenced_module_count.description: This org's modules that declare it in `required_providers`.

version_count.description:
Versions the detail view would list — scanned, or locked by a workspace, or matched by
a module constraint. The same visibility predicate the detail applies, so the list
never advertises more versions than the detail shows.

mirrored_count.description: Of those versions, how many are mirrored upstream artefacts.

published_count.description:
Of those versions, how many this org publishes — including ones served by substitution
from a platform build that wrote no row into this org's catalog.

latest_version.description:
Newest of `version_count` by semver. `null` when none are visible. Computed by semver
rather than `released_at` or SQL ordering, both of which mis-rank (`'1.9.0' > '1.10.0'`
lexically).

upstream_latest_version.description:
The registry's newest release, floored at the newest version we demonstrably hold —
the catalog is legitimately ahead of the cached pointer between refresh ticks, so a
pointer below it is wrong rather than stale. `null` until something resolves it, which
clients should render as "not resolved yet" rather than as a version.

vuln_count.description:
Findings on **`latest_version` only** — never an older version's, even where the older
one has findings and the latest does not.

A `0` is therefore not proof of safety: it means the latest version is clean **or**
has not been scanned, and this payload cannot distinguish them. Per-version counts
with an explicit `scanned` flag are on the detail route's `versions[]`
(`ProviderVersionRow`), which is where an absence can be asserted from.

critical_count.description: Critical findings on `latest_version` only. Same caveat as `vuln_count`.

high_count.description: High findings on `latest_version` only. Same caveat as `vuln_count`.

patched_count.description:
Builds that carried CVE fixes. A remediation claim, so tier-gated — reads `0` below the
tier that includes patched builds even where such builds exist.

serve_mode.description:
`off` when the org's tier does not include provider serving — the add succeeds and the
configuration is kept, nothing is advertised.

ProviderVersionRow.title: ProviderVersionRow
ProviderVersionRow.description:
One version of a managed provider. Only versions with a **completed scan** appear; an
unverified version is excluded on purpose and an in-flight build surfaces under
`/provider-flows` instead.

is_published.description: A self-built artifact is published at this version.

released_at.description: Upstream release date, backfilled from the source repository's release tag.

servable.description:
The authorization contract in one field: bytes exist, the version satisfies the org's
constraint, and the org is entitled to it.

has_unfixable_high.description: A high-severity finding with no fixed version available — auto-patch cannot help.

downloads_30d.description: Includes downloads of this version's patched revisions.

build.description: Build/patch state for this version. `null` when none, or when tier-gated.

referenced_by.description: Modules declaring this provider, with the constraint each one asks for.

series_90d.description:
Per-version daily series for the chart, server-capped to the top six versions
plus an `other` bucket.

ProviderScanQueued.title: ProviderScanQueued
ProviderScanQueued.description:
`status: inflight` is a success: a scan for this provider is already running and the work
the caller wanted is already happening.

job_id.description: Present when a new job was queued.

ProviderPatchComparison.title: ProviderPatchComparison
ProviderPatchComparison.description:
The upstream-versus-patched diff for one base version, plus the provenance that makes the
patched binary auditable.

fixed.description: Findings present upstream and absent in the patched revision.

remaining.description: Findings the patch did not address.

report_only_majors.description:
Fixes that would need a major-version bump. Reported, never applied — a major bump can
change provider behaviour.

provenance.description: Exactly which commits produced the patched artifact.

fork_repo.description: Private fork the patch was applied in.

fork_tag.description: Revision tag the patch step created (`v<base>-0.0.<rev>`).

upstream_commit_sha.description: The upstream release commit the patch was applied on top of.

toolchain_bump.description: Go toolchain version set for a standard-library CVE, if any.

servable.description:
Whether following these instructions will work right now. `false` ⇒ warn rather than
hand them over.

steps.description: Ordered commands, each with why it matters.

ProviderBuildOutcome.title: ProviderBuildOutcome
ProviderBuildOutcome.description:
A build request's outcome. Read `status` and the `deduped` / `attached` flags together —
most of these mean no new build was started.

id.description: The build job id, when one was created or attached to.

attached.description: The caller was attached to an in-flight build.

base_version.description: The upstream base that was requested.

rev.description: Revision number allocated to this build.

ProviderAutoPatchOutcome.title: ProviderAutoPatchOutcome
ProviderAutoPatchOutcome.description:
An auto-patch request's outcome. Most statuses are deliberate no-ops, and they are
distinct on purpose: `nothing_to_patch`, `cooling_down` and `abandoned` call for very
different operator responses.

failure_reason.description: Why the base cannot be built, on `unbuildable_base`.

approvers.description: Distinct approvers recorded for this finding.

satisfied.description: `false` ⇒ the build is still blocked; more approvers are needed.

ProviderFlowState.title: ProviderFlowState
ProviderFlowState.description:
Derived pipeline state for one build: the current phase, the step timeline and any failure.

`unknown` is a real, meaningful value: it means the workflow engine could not be reached.
It is never reported as `queued`, because "we cannot see it" and "it is waiting" are
different facts.

phase.description: Current phase, or `unknown` when the engine is unreachable.

requested_via.description: What triggered the build — an operator action, the auto-patch scheduler, or the build cron.

job_id.description: `null` ⇒ no build has ever been attempted for this version.

FormTier.title: FormTier
FormTier.description:
Plan the submitter is interested in. An allowlist rather than free text so the field cannot
be used to inject arbitrary content into the notification email. The empty string is
permitted — it means "unspecified".

PublicFormSubmission.title: PublicFormSubmission
PublicFormSubmission.description: Visitor-supplied, untrusted. Oversized fields are rejected rather than truncated.

email.description: Must contain `@`. Not verified — this is a contact form, not a sign-up.

metadata.description:
The enterprise quote form's structured answers. When present it is stored as JSON in
place of `use_case`.

examples.name: Dana Okafor
examples.use_case: Private module registry for 40 engineers, with CI-driven state.

R2EventPayload.title: R2EventPayload
R2EventPayload.description:
Either shape R2 emits. Keys outside
`modules/{namespace}/{name}/{provider}/{version}.tar.gz` are ignored.

eventName.description: Only names containing `ObjectCreated` or `PutObject` are acted on.

OkMessage.title: OkMessage
OkMessage.description: An acknowledgement with human-readable confirmation text.

ReasonRequest.title: ReasonRequest
ReasonRequest.description:
A mandatory human justification for an action that overrides a machine verdict. Stored with
the acting user; some surfaces return it to consumers in the refusal text.

examples.reason: Accepted for the 2026-10-12 hotfix; CVE is not reachable in our call path.

reason.description: Recorded with the override. Expected when setting one.

examples.reason: Superseded by v2; stop new consumers.

ModuleVersionsResponse.title: ModuleVersionsResponse
ModuleVersionsResponse.description: The Registry Protocol v1 version list. Shape is dictated by the protocol.

ModulePolicyResult.title: ModulePolicyResult
ModulePolicyResult.description: One policy's verdict against one version.

failure_msg.description: Why it failed. `null` when it passed.

ModuleSeveritySummary.title: ModuleSeveritySummary
ModuleSeveritySummary.description: Finding counts by severity for one version.

ModuleVcsProvenance.title: ModuleVcsProvenance
ModuleVcsProvenance.description:
Where this version was published from. Populated only for a publish authenticated by VCS
OIDC trust — every field is `null` for a token publish. `vcs_commit_url` is constructed
server-side from a host allowlist; it is never taken from the token.

ModuleVersionSummary.title: ModuleVersionSummary
ModuleVersionSummary.description:
Version metadata without the heavy fields (README, findings, policy verdicts). What a list
renders.

published_at.description: ISO 8601. Note the detail surfaces use ISO here, not epoch millis.

download_url.description: Present only where the service computed one.

module_id.description:
The module instance's id. This is the `instance_key` for a per-instance policy
override, which is why it is exposed rather than kept internal.

consumable.description: Policy verdict. `false` means an enforcing policy failed.

consumable_override.description: An owner has overridden the policy verdict for this version.

ModuleScanStatus.title: ModuleScanStatus
ModuleScanStatus.description:
A version's publish lifecycle. Only `published` is resolvable by the registry protocol;
`failed` means the scan itself failed, which is distinct from a policy block.

ModuleSearchHit.title: ModuleSearchHit
ModuleSearchHit.description:
One module, represented by its latest published version plus module-level rollups.
`scan_status` is always `published` by construction — the hit *is* the latest published
version — and is included so a client can hand it straight to a status badge.

deprecated.description: True if the module **or** its latest version is deprecated.

downloads.description: Download events across all versions of the module.

version_count.description: Published versions only, so it agrees with `version`.

next_offset.description: Offset for the next page, or `null` on the last one.

ModulePublishPending.title: ModulePublishPending
ModulePublishPending.description: Default publish acknowledgement. The scan has been enqueued, not finished.

storage_key.description: Object-storage key the archive was streamed to.

ModulePublishSettled.description:
Returned for `wait=true` when the scan settled inside the budget: the acknowledgement
merged with the full version detail, so CI can assert on findings without a second call.

ModulePublishTimedOut.title: ModulePublishTimedOut
ModulePublishTimedOut.description:
`202`. The archive is stored and the scan is running — it has not failed. Poll
`GET …/{version}/status`.

ProviderVersionsResponse.title: ProviderVersionsResponse
ProviderVersionsResponse.description:
The provider registry protocol's version list. Shape is dictated by the protocol: each
entry carries the protocol versions and platforms that version supports, so the client can
pick a platform before requesting a download document.

ProviderDownloadPayload.title: ProviderDownloadPayload
ProviderDownloadPayload.description:
The provider registry protocol's download document. `download_url`, `shasums_url` and
`shasums_signature_url` are HMAC-signed, short-lived URLs on this host — `tofu` fetches
them without an `Authorization` header, so the signature is the credential.

`signing_keys` is what makes the chain verifiable: a mirrored version carries the upstream
publisher's key, a self-built one carries the Terramantle platform key.

StateLockRequest.title: StateLockRequest
StateLockRequest.description:
Terraform's lock info, as the `http` backend sends it. Field names are Terraform's
(capitalised) and are stored verbatim for display.

ID.description: Lock id. A random one is generated when absent.

StateLock.title: StateLock
StateLock.description:
A held lock. The actor-origin fields (`actor_ip`, `actor_country`, `actor_city`,
`actor_name`, `info`) are **omitted for a `reader`** — they are personal data. They are
display and audit only and never feed an authorization decision.

StateVcsProvenance.title: StateVcsProvenance
StateVcsProvenance.description:
Where a push came from. Populated only for a push authenticated by VCS OIDC trust; all
`null` otherwise. `vcs_commit_url` is built server-side from a host allowlist.

blocked.description:
`1` ⇒ the policy gate will reject the next apply's `LOCK` until an admin attests.
An integer rather than a boolean because it is the raw indexed column.

real_resource_count.description: Real managed resources. `null` ⇒ not yet classified.

internal_resource_count.description: Terraform-internal resources (data sources, nulls). `null` ⇒ not classified.

pushed_by.description:
Legacy `users.id` foreign key — `null` for every bot-token push, which is most CI
pushes. Read `actor_type` / `actor_name` instead.

push_duration_ms.description: `LOCK` → push duration for the apply that produced this version. `null` ⇒ unmeasured.

promoted_from_serial.description: Set when this version is a restore. `null` for a normal apply.

window_days.description: Echoed so a caption never hardcodes the window.

pushes.description: One entry per UTC day with at least one push. Sparse — the client zero-fills.

StateGraphNode.title: StateGraphNode
StateGraphNode.description:
Node ids are namespaced by kind — `ws:{id}`, `prov:{namespace}/{type}`,
`mod:{namespace}/{name}/{provider}` — so a single id space holds all three without
collision. Which optional fields are present depends on `kind`.

discovered.description:
Provider nodes: auto-discovered from a lock file or module scan, versus added by hand.
A node present only because something locks it is discovered by definition.

outdated.description: Provider nodes: some workspace pins an older version than its constraint allows.

blocked.description: Workspace nodes: the policy gate will reject the next apply.

rel.description: `locks` = workspace → provider (from a lock file). `requires` = module → provider.

lock_file.description: `null` when no lock file has been uploaded.

truncated.description: The provider list hit its row cap and was trimmed.

WorkspaceProvider.title: WorkspaceProvider
WorkspaceProvider.description: One provider pinned by the workspace's lock file, with scan rollups.

constraints.description: Version constraint from the lock file.

latest_version.description: Newest upstream version, from the global latest-version cache.

latest_matching.description: Newest version satisfying `constraints`. Drives the drift indicator.

current_scan.description: `null` ⇒ NOT scanned. An empty rollup ⇒ scanned and clean.

latest_scan.description: `null` when there is no `latest_version`, or it has no completed scan.

VersionScanRollup.title: VersionScanRollup
VersionScanRollup.description:
Finding counts for one provider version, from the cross-org scan cache. Only completed
scans are represented, which is why an absent entry means "not scanned".

version_id.description: The NEW version the restore created.

idempotent_replay.description: Present and `true` when this is a replay of an earlier call with the same key.

version_id.description: The NEW version written with the resources removed.

removed.description: `null` on an idempotent replay — the removal already happened.

StateResourceTree.title: StateResourceTree
StateResourceTree.description:
Managed resources as a tree. Addresses and structural metadata only — no resource values
are ever returned. The `compare_*` fields are populated when `?compare=` was supplied.

get.description:
What `terraform` and `tofu` fetch before any module or provider operation, to learn where
each protocol lives.

`providers.v1` is **host-dependent**. On the bare host it is the token-resolved base; on
`{orgSlug}.registry.terramantle.dev` it is `/v1/providers/{orgSlug}/`, so the client
appends provider sources to the org-scoped route. The subdomain is a path hint only —
advertising a base for an unknown slug is harmless because membership is enforced at the
route. Modules stay slug-in-path on both hosts and so never change here.

What the `terramantle` CLI fetches from its configured API base **before it holds any
token**, so the issuer, the audiences and the public device-flow client are resolved from
the deployment rather than compiled into the binary. Also tells `terramantle console`
which portal to open.

Every value is public: a device-flow client carries no secret. Each field is overridable
client-side via the matching `TERRAMANTLE_*` environment variable.

What the React portal fetches at boot, before it constructs its OIDC client, so the
authority and client id come from the deployment instead of the bundle — a stale build-time
value has white-screened the app before. All values are public; a PKCE client holds no
secret.

get.description:
Returns the requested status code and reflects the query string back in the body. It exists
so the state-sample demo repo's `echo` stack has a dependable endpoint instead of a public
third-party one; a per-run nonce in the query makes the stored response change every apply

Unauthenticated, because `tofu apply` calls it with no token.

post.description:
Called by the module scanner when a scan finishes. Writes findings, the severity summary,
the README and usage example, the policy verdicts, the dependency edges, and the providers
the module declares in `required_providers` — which is how a provider becomes a discovered
artefact.

**Forward-only.** A late or duplicate `failed` report cannot clobber a version that already
reached `published`; the update is guarded on the version still being in flight. That
matters because a workflow's exit handler and a retried pod can both report.

`category` on a finding is optional while the rollout completes — the Worker derives it
from the tool and rule id when absent.

get.summary: Stream a module archive to the scanner (internal)
get.description:
Streams the stored archive for any module version by id. This is exactly why these routes
fail closed on an unconfigured scanner identity — the route is cross-tenant by design.

404.description: No such version, or the bytes are missing from storage.

post.description:
Called by the state scanner. Writes findings, the optional policy verdicts, and the
recomputed managed-resource split.

**A failing enforcing state policy sets the workspace block here** — which is what the next
apply's `LOCK` is refused on. Verdicts are stored whether or not policies are currently
enabled, so re-enabling re-blocks rather than silently passing.

The resource split is best-effort: absent or `null` leaves the stored columns untouched
rather than erroring, which is also how pre-classification versions get backfilled on a
rescan.

Findings must carry **metadata only** — addresses and counts, never a secret value.

Note this route answers `403` rather than `401` on an auth failure, unlike its siblings.

get.summary: Stream a state file to the scanner (internal)
get.description: Streams the stored state document for any version by id.

404.description: No such version, or the bytes are missing from storage.

post.summary: Ingest one provider version's scan result (internal)
post.description:
One scan job covers several versions and emits **one of these per version**. Results attach
to the job by `job_id`, which is what makes the attachment race-safe when two jobs for the
same provider briefly overlap.

`status` distinguishes three outcomes that must not be conflated:

- `published` — scanned. The result and findings are written.
- `failed` — attempted and failed. Enters the retry tier.
- `skipped` — **never attempted**, because the job ran out of wall-clock budget. No result
  row is written and the backlog marker is re-armed for the next drain tick.

`job_failed: true` is a job-level terminal failure instead — for example a constraint that
matched no versions — and carries none of the per-version fields.

Results land in a **cross-org cache** keyed by provider version, so one scan serves every
org that manages that provider.

The scan pod's first call, and the guard against duplicate queue deliveries doing duplicate
work. The response is two booleans because the three cases need different handling:

| Case | `claimed` | `proceed` | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pending` → claimed | `true` | `true` | This pod owns the job. |
| already `processing` | `false` | `true` | A previous attempt may have died mid-run; re-scanning is safe because per-version ingest is a race-safe upsert. |
| terminal | `false` | `false` | A redelivery after completion. The pod exits `0` and the message is a clean no-op. |

Claiming also starts the reaper's running-time clock — queue time before this point is
unbounded and never reaped.

Mints a short-lived presigned `PUT` so the scanner uploads multi-megabyte SPDX **directly**
— the Worker never buffers it.

The key is identity-addressed by provider version and platform, not namespaced by org or
job, so a version scanned once produces one SBOM every entitled org reads. The provider
identity is resolved from the job rather than taken from the request, because readers
presign `GET`s against the same key and a wrong upstream segment would make the object
vanish.

404.description: No such scan job.

post.description:
Presigns the per-provider clean-hash cache blob: `get` at job start, `put` at job end. One
gzipped JSON object per provider mapping file hash to last-clean time (7-day TTL, enforced
scanner-side); files already in it are left out of the scan shards.

The pod is untrusted and therefore never holds bucket credentials — only this URL. The
blast radius of a poisoned write is bounded by construction: one provider's cache for at
most seven days, after which the periodic rescan tier re-scans every file regardless.

400.description: Invalid JSON, or `job_id` / `method` missing or invalid.

404.description: No such scan job.

get.summary: Fetch a tenant's policies for evaluation (internal)
get.description:
The policies a scanner evaluates against, for one tenant, optionally narrowed to one
artefact kind and instance. Also returns the tenant's missing-signal gate, because the
scanner needs to know whether an absent signal should fail open or closed.

200.description: The policies and the gate setting.

signal_fail_gate.description: Deliberately NOT renamed to `on_missing_signal` with policy-input contract v2, unlike the org settings API. This is an internal wire field read by scanner pods, which deploy on their own schedule — renaming it would create a deploy-order hazard (a worker ahead of its scanners, or behind them) for no reader-facing gain. The POLICY INPUT the scanner then builds does use the new name.

get.summary: Shared reference data for policy evaluation (internal)
get.description:
Facts about the WORLD that policies evaluate artefacts against, as opposed to facts about
the artefact itself. Today that is CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue.

This is deliberately not part of the policy input. OPA has two document roots: `input` is
the artefact under evaluation, `data` is what a policy may consult about it. A CVE
catalogue is identical for every artefact, so copying it into every `input` would bloat
each evaluation for no gain — and `data.terramantle.ref.kev[cve]` is how Rego expects a
lookup like this to read. The scanner fetches this once per job and mounts it as `data`;
the policy-bundle path ships the same document inside the bundle.

`kev` is an ARRAY on the wire — compact and ordered, so it diffs cleanly — which the
scanner converts into the object Rego needs for a membership test.

`kev_fetched_at` is null when the mirror has never been populated. That is reported rather
than hidden: a policy that read an empty catalogue as "nothing is exploited" would fail
open, so the consumer is told the difference between "nothing is listed" and "we do not
know yet".

kev.description: CVE ids on the CISA KEV catalogue, sorted.

aliases.description: GHSA-… / GO-… to CVE-… . Scanner findings carry trivy's VulnerabilityID, which for Go dependencies is often not a CVE, while KEV and EPSS are CVE-keyed — without this map an alias-keyed finding silently fails to match either.

kev_fetched_at.description: Epoch ms the document was built; null when never.

get.description:
The reference data as an OPA bundle rooted at `terramantle/ref`, so a policy evaluated by
the opa-gate service reads `data.terramantle.ref.*` exactly as the scanners do.

ONE bundle, shared by every tenant — it carries no customer data. It is deliberately
separate from the per-org policy bundles, which are content-addressed on policy TEXT:
reference data inside one of those would either churn every org's revision daily or go
stale until somebody edited a policy.

**This endpoint never returns a non-bundle, and that is a deliberate difference from
`/bundles/{tenant}/{rev}` next to it.** opa-gate's readiness probe gates on every configured
bundle having activated, and regresses when a previously-good one starts failing — so two
replicas go NotReady, the worker cannot reach OPA, and the plan gate fails closed for every
org. The org route can safely 404 because its pointer and object are written together; here
a revision can outlive its object, so a miss rebuilds the current document inline instead.
The bundle served may therefore carry a different revision than the one requested; OPA
activates what it is given and the discovery poll converges it.

parameters.name: rev
parameters.description: Content-addressed revision, from the discovery document's `bundles.ref.resource`.

200.description: The gzipped bundle. `Cache-Control: immutable` when served from storage (the revision is in the URL, so those bytes never change); `no-store` on the rebuilt fallback.

post.summary: Record build gate verdicts without changing job status (internal)
post.description:
Stores the gate verdicts for a build, including FAILING ones, and touches nothing else.

`/complete` also stores verdicts, but the Workflow only reaches it once every gate has
passed — the gate barrier exits non-zero otherwise, and `finalize` depends on it. So D1
has only ever held passing verdicts, and a blocked build stored no reasons at all: they
lived in the Workflow CR and the pod log, neither of which is queryable.

That was not only a forensics gap. The two-person override validates a submitted
`finding_hash` against the findings of FAILED gates — a passed gate needs no override — so
with only passing verdicts stored, that set was empty for exactly the builds an override
exists for, and every approval was rejected as not matching an open finding.

Called by the gate step immediately before it exits non-zero. Upserts on `(job_id, gate)`,
the same key `/complete` uses, so a retry that passes replaces the blocked verdict rather
than colliding with it.

gate_verdicts.description: Verdicts as the gate runner produced them. Entries without a string `gate` and a boolean `passed` are skipped rather than rejecting the whole report — a partial record beats none when a build is already failing.

post.summary: Report that a build has started (internal)
post.description:
Transitions a build job out of `pending`. `transitioned: false` means the row had already
moved on — a duplicate or late report, not an error.

The build pipeline's terminal report: which platforms were produced, the gate verdicts, the
patch provenance, and the registry lineage the artifacts were published under.

Two things here are load-bearing:

- **`attempt` is the retry discriminator.** A report whose attempt is *higher* than the
  stored row's is a genuine retry and re-opens a terminal row; an equal-or-lower attempt is
  a duplicate and is ignored by the forward-only guard. That guard exists because the
  workflow's exit handler and a retried pod can both report for the same job.
- **`source_upstream` is required on success and must match the job row's lineage.** A
  mismatch is refused with `lineage_mismatch`, because the lineage is part of the published
  object key — accepting a mismatch would publish bytes where nothing will look for them.

`status: "failed"` is the exit handler's path: `patch_provenance` then carries the failure
stage and reason instead of git provenance.

200.description: Recorded, or ignored as a duplicate.

400.description:
`job_id` missing, required success fields missing, `source_upstream` missing, or
`lineage_mismatch` — the report's lineage disagrees with the job row's.

example.message: job is terraform.io lineage, report says opentofu.org

404.description: No such build job.

post.description:
The queue supervisor's reconcile tick: a heartbeat plus the observed workflow state for
each claim it holds. This is what fills the live build-flow view and what the reapers
reason about.

Three details carry weight:

- **The heartbeat fires every tick, even with zero claims.** Its *absence* is how the
  reapers tell "no workflow" from "no observer" — without it they cannot distinguish a lost
  workflow from a supervisor that is simply down.
- **`at_capacity`** says the pull loop is paused at its claim ceiling, so an unleased
  message may be legitimate queued work. Absence-based reaping has to pause too.
- **`observed_at` is the ordering guard.** The Worker compares it against the stored
  timestamp and drops out-of-order events, so a slow tick cannot overwrite newer state.

`applied` / `ignored` report how many events passed and failed that guard.

ignored.description: Events dropped by the out-of-order guard.

post.description:
The org-agnostic counterpart of the per-org rescan, for operator tooling. Resolves the
owning org itself rather than taking one on trust.

`status: "inflight"` means a scan is already running for that provider and nothing new was
queued. For a self-built revision, only a **published** revision can be scanned — anything
else is `409`, and a revision whose lineage is not a public registry is `422`.

404.description: No org manages this provider, or no self-built revision with that version.

409.description: The revision is not published, so it cannot be scanned.

422.description: Unsupported upstream, or the source repository is unresolvable.

post.description:
Operator-triggered build, resolving the owning org itself. `org_id` may be supplied to
attribute the build explicitly.

Pass the upstream base version (`X.Y.Z`), never a revision — the revision scheme is
`<base>-0.0.<rev>` and the pipeline allocates the revision. `status: "fleet_saturated"`
reports the fleet depth and the ceiling; nothing was queued.

org_id.description: Org id or slug to attribute the build to.

200.description: Deduplicated, already entitled, or the fleet is saturated.

400.description: A revision was passed instead of an `X.Y.Z` base.

404.description: No org has a registry artefact for this provider, or no such org.

post.description:
Returns a build job wedged in an in-flight state to a retryable one, freeing the global
in-flight dedup slot so the base can build again. The manual counterpart of the reaper.

Clears a lineage row stuck in `building` so its base can be built again, **without
charging the base's failure cooldown** — the build never really ran, so it should not count
against it.

post.summary: Backfill serve mode on discovered providers (internal/operator)
post.description:
One-shot migration helper: moves existing discovered provider rows into `serve` for orgs
entitled to serve, matching what auto-serve-on-discovery now does for new rows. Never
rewrites a row whose serve mode was set deliberately.

200.description: Backfilled. The body reports what changed.

post.description:
Recomputes the consumable flag from stored policy verdicts. The repair path for artefacts
whose verdicts and flags drifted apart — after a bug, or a migration that changed how a
verdict is interpreted.

post.summary: Refresh reference data and republish its OPA bundle (internal/operator)
post.description:
Runs the same work as the daily reference-data cron on demand: refresh the CISA KEV, EPSS,
CVE-alias and SPDX mirrors, then publish a new global reference bundle if the content moved.

Exists because the refreshes and the publish share ONE daily schedule, so there is otherwise
no way to populate `data.terramantle.ref` except waiting for it — and a local
`--test-scheduled` cannot stand in, because scheduled triggering does not reach a deployed
Worker. Needed on the day the feature ships, and whenever stored data is WRONG rather than
merely stale (lowering the EPSS floor means re-reading the whole feed).

Mutating and **global** in scope — this data is shared by every tenant, not per-org.

Safe to re-run. The publish refuses to replace a good bundle with an implausibly small
catalogue, because an empty one still looks authoritative to Rego: a `deny` that tests
`data.terramantle.ref.kev[cve]` simply stops matching, which is a silent fail-OPEN that the
gate's readiness probe cannot detect.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description:
Bypass BOTH short-circuits: each source's internal TTL gate and the publish's revision
compare. Without it, a call made soon after a successful one is a no-op — the right
default for a retry, but not for "the stored data is wrong, re-read it".

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description:
Comma-separated subset of `kev,epss,aliases,spdx` (default: all). EPSS is much the
heaviest, and one invocation has a fixed CPU and subrequest budget, so a combined run
that fails can be retried one source at a time. The publish always runs regardless,
since skipping it would leave refreshed rows invisible to OPA.

200.description:
Refreshed. `refreshed` carries each source's own result (a source whose TTL had not
expired reports `refreshed: false`), and `published` reports the bundle outcome —
including `reason: unchanged` when the content did not move and `reason: implausible`
when the plausibility floor refused the publish.

post.description:
Fills missing size columns for module archives or state objects by reading them back from
storage.

Mutating and **all-tenant** in scope, so confirm the scanner client id is configured in
production before invoking — without it the auth check falls back to accepting any bot or
the static secret.

get.description:
Streams a content-addressed OPA bundle for one org at one revision. Fetched by the OPA gate
with the same `opa-gate`-scoped token it uses for discovery.

Content-addressed, so a revision's bytes never change — which is what lets OPA cache them
and lets discovery hand out a revision id without a cache-invalidation protocol.

parameters.name: rev
parameters.description: Content-addressed revision. Immutable.

get.summary: Serve the OPA discovery bundle for every org (internal)
get.description:
A gzipped tar holding one `data.json` that is itself an OPA config fragment: one shared
storage service entry, plus one bundle entry per org carrying a freshly presigned URL for
that org's **current** content-addressed bundle.

OPA's native discovery polls this and reconciles its loaded bundles to match on every poll,
so a new or changed org's bundle appears automatically — no per-org endpoint, and no
bespoke reconciliation loop on either side. That is the whole reason it is one document
rather than a listing API.

Fails **closed**: without a valid `opa-gate`-scoped token this is `401`, never a partial or
empty bundle set — an empty set would silently disable every org's policy gate.

503.description: Policy-bundle storage or presign configuration is missing.

get.summary: Stream the redacted plan render to the plan scanner (internal)
get.description:
Streams the stored plan render — which is the **redacted** one, because redaction happened
at ingest before anything was persisted. So no plan value leaves the Worker even toward the
scanner, and the scanner's findings are metadata-only by construction rather than by
convention.

404.description: No such version, or the render is missing from storage.

post.description:
Called by the plan scanner after enriching a redacted render with drift, replacement-cause
and secret-count insights.

Replaces the version's findings and its **advisory** policy rows atomically, while
**preserving the synchronous built-in gate row**. That asymmetry is the point: a rescan must
never overwrite the enforcing decision that was made at ingest and that an apply may
already have been refused on.

Findings carry metadata only — addresses, attribute paths and counts, never a concrete
value.

get.description:
The signed-in user's record, with no side effects. `404` means the token is valid but the
user has never registered — call `POST /api/auth/me` first.

404.description: Valid token, unregistered user.

example.message: User not registered - call POST /api/auth/me first

post.summary: Register or fetch the current user
post.description:
Called by the portal immediately after an OIDC login completes. Idempotent — safe to call
on every login, and the intended way to seed client state.

A first login also provisions: a personal org with a generated name, a set of default OPA
policies for it, and a welcome email. Policy seeding is best-effort and never blocks
registration.

`422` means the token carried no `email` claim, which the platform cannot work without:
RBAC resolves membership by email. Request the `email` scope.

200.description:
Registered, or already registered. `is_new_user` distinguishes the two — it is what
drives first-run onboarding.

example.message: Email claim not found in token.

get.description:
Every org the caller is a member of, with their role in each. A personal org always
reports `starter` regardless of what is stored — a personal tenant cannot hold a paid tier.

404.description: The caller has no user record yet.

post.description:
Creates an org with the caller as `owner`, and returns the full org shape so the client can
use it without a refetch.

`tier` other than `starter` is accepted here only while the beta offer stands; otherwise a
paid tier needs checkout and this returns `403`. `policy_preset` seeds the new org's policy
enablement, and anything other than `off` is recorded in the billing audit log so the
policies tab can show what the wizard applied.

policy_preset.description: Which default policies to enable. `off` seeds none.

403.description: A paid tier was requested and checkout is required.

delete.description:
`owner` only. Personal and demo orgs cannot be deleted — a personal org is the user's own
account and a demo org is shared, so both refuse with `403`.

403.description: Not an owner, or a personal/demo org.

example.message: Personal organizations cannot be deleted

get.description:
Active members only, oldest first. The demo org refuses this with `403` — its membership is
every trial user, which is not a list any of them should see.
