post.description:
Invites an **existing** user by email — they must have logged in at least once, so there is
a record to attach the membership to. Re-adding someone who previously left reactivates
their row and consumes a seat; re-roling an active member does not.

403.description: Insufficient role, or the demo org.

404.description: No user with that email — they must log in first.

patch.description: Cannot leave the org without an owner — demoting the last one is refused.

409.description: Would leave the org with no owner.

delete.description: Removing the last owner is refused.

409.description: Would leave the org with no owner.

delete.description:
Removes the caller's own membership. Human only — a machine identity has no membership to
give up. The last owner cannot leave.

409.description: The caller is the last owner.

post.summary: Claim an email domain for the org
post.description:
Claims a domain so future sign-ups with a matching email address join this org
automatically. `owner` only.

get.description:
Metadata and scopes only — a client secret is shown once, at creation or rotation, and is
never stored or returned again. `last_used_at` and the geo fields are throttled to one
write per identity per five minutes, so they are "recently seen", not exact.

post.description:
Provisions an OIDC `client_credentials` identity in the IdP and records it against the org.

**`client_secret` is returned exactly once, here.** It is never stored, so it cannot be
recovered — a lost secret means rotating the token.

Three scopes:

- `global` — every org the creator administers. Write on modules.
- `org` — this org only, with `include_modules` and `include_state` controlling read vs
  write per domain.
- `state_workspaces` — this org, but state access only on the workspaces named in
  `state_grants`, each with its own permission. This is what a per-pipeline CI token
  should use.

delete.description: Deletes the IdP client as well as the record. Tokens already issued stop validating.

post.description:
Issues a new secret and invalidates the old one. `member` and above, **human only** —
a compromised token must not be able to rotate itself into a fresh one.

The new secret is returned once.

get.summary: List every token the caller administers
get.description:
Cross-org: every machine token belonging to an org where the caller is `owner` or `admin`,
plus any global tokens they created themselves. Newest first.

This is the "where are my credentials" view — the per-org list cannot answer it for someone
who administers several orgs.

404.description: The caller has no user record yet.

get.summary: Get plan, limits, usage and grace period
get.description:
Everything the billing page needs in one call: the effective tier, the feature matrix for
it, current usage against the counted limits, and whether a downgrade grace period is
running.

A personal org always reports `starter`. `grace_period` is `null` when none is set; when
present, `active` is whether it is still running.

Requires billing access — `owner`, `admin`, or a member flagged `is_billing_admin` — on top
of the `member` role.

403.description: No billing access for this caller.

example.message: Billing access required

get.description:
The feature half of `GET …/billing`, readable by **any** org member — the portal needs to
know whether to render the provider or state tabs without granting everyone billing access.

post.description:
Returns a URL to redirect the browser to. A personal org cannot be upgraded — create a real
org first — and `starter` is not a checkout target.

403.description: No billing access, or a personal org.

post.description: Returns a URL where the customer manages their existing subscription.

post.summary: Switch tier without payment (beta offer, ended)
post.description:
The beta free-tier offer. **This endpoint now returns `410` unconditionally** — use
checkout. It is kept so an old client bundle gets an explanatory refusal instead of a bare
`404`.

example.message: The beta free-tier offer has ended. Use checkout to change plan.

patch.summary: Grant or revoke a member's billing access
patch.description:
`owner` only. Lets a `member` reach the billing endpoints without promoting them to `admin`
across the whole org.

404.description: Not a member of this org.

get.description:
Every governance-relevant action: membership changes, token lifecycle, policy settings,
serve overrides, state force-unlocks and promotions, provider build decisions. Newest
first.

Page either by `offset` or by `before` (a timestamp cursor). `before` wins when both are
given, and is the right choice for a log that is still being appended to — an offset
shifts under you.

Requires billing access, and the retention window depends on the tier.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Restrict to one action.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description:
Timestamp cursor in epoch milliseconds — return events older than this. Takes
precedence over `offset`.

403.description: No billing access for this caller.

get.summary: List the org's VCS trust entries
get.description:
Which CI identities may authenticate as this org without a stored secret. The matched
entry is what resolves a GitHub/GitLab OIDC token to an org.

post.description:
Registers a `sub` pattern from GitHub Actions or GitLab CI. A pipeline whose OIDC token
matches then authenticates as this org with no long-lived credential anywhere.

`subject` is matched against the token's `sub`, so it should be as specific as the pipeline
allows — `repo:acme/infra:ref:refs/heads/main` rather than `repo:acme/*`. Overlap is
policed: an entry that overlaps another org's ambiguously is refused, and at authentication
time a `sub` matching several entries resolves to the most specific one or fails closed.

CI identities are bots: capped at `member` and refused on human-only actions, whatever the
trust entry says.

subject.description: Pattern matched against the OIDC token's `sub`.

409.description:
This entry already exists, or it overlaps an existing one in a way that would make
authentication ambiguous.

example.message: This trust entry already exists

delete.description: Pipelines relying on it stop authenticating immediately.

get.description:
The dashboard payload: download and apply totals and series, top modules and actors, state
statistics, open findings by severity with per-artifact drill-downs, the riskiest modules
and workspaces, slow applies, workspace runtimes, an infrastructure footprint, and
continuous-patching exposure — vulnerable superseded versions still being downloaded.

Most series cover 30 days; the per-module and per-workspace series cover 90. One call
rather than a dozen, because the dashboard renders it all at once.

get.summary: Get the cross-org module dependency graph
get.description:
Modules the caller can see, and the dependencies between them. Dependencies outside their
visibility appear as stub nodes with zero counts — the edge is real and worth drawing even
when the target is not readable.

Not org-scoped: this is deliberately the caller's whole visible surface, which is what makes
a shared module's blast radius visible across orgs.

404.description: The caller has no user record yet.

put.summary: Ingest a redacted terraform plan (plan protocol)
put.description:
Upload a `terraform show -json` plan render for a state workspace. The path `key`
is the state workspace key (everything before the required `.tfplan` suffix; it may
contain slashes). Plans reuse the state workspace — no separate plan workspace — and
share the state push permission model: a machine client token (or a human with
`write`) on that workspace only.

The request body is the raw `terraform show -json` output. It is REDACTED
server-side (`lib/tfplan.ts`) before any persistence: `before`/`after`/`sensitive`
values never reach D1, R2, or any response. The server derives action counts,
drift/replacement/sensitive counts, hashes the redacted canonical JSON
(`attestation_hash`), stores the redacted render to R2, and inserts a
`plan_versions` row. Idempotent by (workspace, `plan_ref`, `attestation_hash`): a
byte-identical re-PUT returns the existing version.

On ingest the synchronous M2 policy gate runs inline (and the M6 custom-Rego gate
when the org has plan Rego); a violation sets `state_workspaces.blocked` BEFORE the
200 is returned, so the next apply's LOCK is rejected. An async plan-scan job is
best-effort enqueued for advisory insights.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org slug.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description:
State workspace key, WITHOUT the `.tfplan` suffix. May contain slashes (the
router wildcard captures the full key).

parameters.name: X-Plan-Ref
parameters.description:
Concurrent-plan discriminator (PR / branch / SHA). NULL = default/mainline.
Two open PRs against one workspace are separated by this.

parameters.name: X-Plan-Prior-Serial
parameters.description:
The prior state serial the plan was made against (`show -json` does not reliably
expose it, so it is read from this header). Digits only; anything else is treated
as absent. Drives the staleness check.

parameters.name: X-Plan-Prior-Lineage
parameters.description: The prior state lineage UUID the plan was made against.

parameters.name: Content-Length
parameters.description: Checked early; a plan larger than 100MB is rejected with 413.

requestBody.description: Raw `terraform show -json` output (redacted server-side before persist).

schema.description:
A `terraform show -json` plan document. Its concrete values are stripped at
ingest; the shape is Terraform's and is not re-documented here.

200.description: Plan ingested (or an idempotent match returned).

version_id.description: Primary key of the plan_versions row.

402.description: Tenant plan/tier quota exceeded (state-backend quota gate).

get.summary: List plan version history for a workspace
get.description: Redacted plan version history, newest first. HUMAN/UI surface — tenant `reader`+.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size (1–100, default 50).

get.summary: Get one plan version's summary + redacted findings
get.description:
The version summary plus its redacted findings. `tool` is omitted from findings
(kept internal, mirroring the state projection). Tenant `reader`+.

post.summary: Manually approve a gated plan version
post.description:
Escape hatch for a plan-triggered LOCK-gate block. Writes a one-shot override bound
to this exact (`plan_version_id`, `attestation_hash`) and clears the workspace block
ONLY if this plan raised it (approving plan A never clears a block plan B raised).
Tenant `admin`+ AND HUMAN only — a bot / OIDC CI token cannot self-approve
(two-person control).

reason.description: Free-text approval reason (defaults to "Manual plan approval").

cleared.description: Whether a workspace block was actually cleared by this approval.

get.summary: Get persisted policy-evaluation results for a plan version
get.description:
The persisted gate verdicts: the synchronous built-in M2 gate (`source: builtin`)
plus any async advisory OPA verdicts (`source: opa`). Redacted-safe — `failure_msg`
carries gate reasons only, never a plan value. This is what the UI Policy tab reads
instead of deriving a verdict from the `blocked` flag. Tenant `reader`+.

The verdict a CI apply job curls BEFORE `terraform apply` to prove the plan it is
about to apply is the reviewed one. FAIL-CLOSED contract (also stated in the
response `reason`): a CI gate MUST require `attested && approved && !stale`. An
unknown hash returns `attested: false`, so a swapped/rehashed plan can never pass.
Tenant `reader`+.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: Lowercase sha-256 hex digest of the redacted plan JSON.

get.description:
Same verdict as the hash endpoint, keyed by a known plan version (the UI renders the
Summary/Drift attestation status from this). Resolves the version's hash and
delegates to the same fail-closed check. Tenant `reader`+.

Org-level rollup (M5 signature USP). Groups the org's recent plan forced-replacements
(delete+create) by provider and reports the affected workspaces plus each provider's
blast radius (workspaces using it at all, via the provider-usage join). Value-free —
sourced from redacted plan findings. A single static segment, so it never collides
with the `/{workspace}/*` routes. Tenant `reader`+.

get.summary: Get the org-level default gate config
get.description: The org-level default gate config (`null` if unset). Tenant `admin`+.

put.summary: Upsert the org-level default gate config
put.description: Upsert the org-level default gate config. Tenant `admin`+.

get.summary: Get the per-workspace gate config override
get.description: The per-workspace gate config override (`null` if unset). Tenant `admin`+.

put.summary: Upsert the per-workspace gate config override
put.description:
Upsert the per-workspace gate config override (per-workspace wins over the org
default). Tenant `admin`+.

get.summary: Get the policy input JSON Schema
get.description:
The JSON Schema for the `input` document a Rego policy is evaluated against, for every
artefact kind. Generated from the Worker's own types, so it is the authority for policy
authors — not a restatement.

Pure documentation with no tenant data, so it is unauthenticated and cacheable (5 minutes).
It powers the `?` helper in the Rego editor and the integration guide.

get.summary: Get one artefact's policy input schema
get.description:
A self-contained schema for one artefact kind's `input` — no cross-references to resolve,
so an editor can load just the shape it needs.

404.description: Unknown artefact kind, or no schema available for it.

get.summary: Get policy enablement and blocked counts
get.description:
The enablement snapshot plus how much is currently blocked, which is what makes a toggle
safe to flip: an admin can see the blast radius before enabling enforcement.

`opaTier` is the tier gate. Enforcement needs it **and** the relevant toggle, so
`global: true` with `opaTier: false` evaluates and reports but blocks nothing.

patch.description:
Flips the global master switch, the per-artefact switches, and the missing-signal gate.
Send only the keys you are changing.

**Flipping a toggle recomputes consumability across the org and can enqueue rescans.** Two
consequences visible in the response:

- A request that changes nothing is a true no-op: it returns the current state with
  `changed: false` and `rows_changed: 0`, and performs no recompute, rescan or audit write.
- A request that *does* change something is rate limited — a second flip inside the
  cooldown returns `429`. That debounce is why this is `PATCH` with a delta rather than a
  whole-object `PUT`.

`on_missing_signal` decides how a **missing** trust signal is treated: `ignore` fails open,
`hard_fail` fails closed. It is the single most consequential field here.

schema.description: Only the keys present are considered; a key whose value already matches is ignored.

global.description: Master switch. Off ⇒ nothing is enforced for any artefact kind.

failClosed.summary: Treat a missing trust signal as a failure

200.description:
The resulting settings. `changed: false` means the request was a no-op — nothing was
recomputed and nothing was audited.

429.description:
Settings were changed very recently. The cooldown exists because each real change
triggers an org-wide recompute.

example.message: Policy settings were changed very recently; try again shortly.

get.description:
Filterable by artefact kind. An artefact-scoped read also carries the compliance rollup
(`eval_failing`, `eval_total`, `eval_failing_names`) so the list can show what each policy
is currently blocking without a second call; an unscoped read omits it.

post.description:
The Rego **must** declare `package terramantle.policy` — the evaluator looks for its rules
there, so a different package would silently never fire. That is rejected at `400` rather
than accepted and ignored.

`artefact_type` is validated against the known kinds rather than coerced, so a typo cannot
file a policy under the wrong tab. Leaving it out defaults to `module`.

`instance_key` decides the policy's reach:

- absent ⇒ an **org baseline**, applying to every artefact of that kind and inheritable;
- set ⇒ **identity-custom**, attached to exactly one artefact identity (a module id, a
  state workspace, a provider, a plan workspace key). `artefact_type` is then required,
  because an instance key means nothing without knowing what kind of instance it names.

Creating a policy enqueues a bundle rebuild for the org.

is_enforcing.description: `false` (the default) records verdicts without blocking anything.

instance_key.description: Set for an identity-custom policy. Requires `artefact_type`.

value.name: no-public-ingress

400.description:
Missing `name`/`rego`, a Rego body that does not declare `package terramantle.policy`,
an unknown `artefact_type`, or an `instance_key` with no `artefact_type`.

get.summary: List the policies in force for one artefact identity
get.description:
The effective set for a single artefact — org baselines plus any identity-custom policies —
which is what an artefact's policy tab renders. Both parameters are required: an instance
key means nothing without its artefact kind.

parameters.name: instance_key
parameters.description:
The artefact identity — a module id, a state workspace name, a provider key, or a plan
workspace key, depending on `artefact_type`.

post.summary: Enable or disable every policy for one artefact identity
post.description:
Bulk switch across all policies affecting one artefact — the "turn this artefact's gate off"
action, rather than toggling each policy by hand. `affected` is how many override rows
changed.

patch.description:
Send only the fields to change. A new `rego` body must still declare
`package terramantle.policy`.

The response carries `rescan` alongside the policy: changing a policy means existing
artefacts' verdicts are stale, so the Worker coalesces and enqueues the re-evaluation and
tells you what it queued. A policy edit is never silently retroactive-but-unapplied.

200.description: Updated, with what was queued for re-evaluation.

delete.description:
Removes the policy and its verdicts, and enqueues a bundle rebuild. Artefacts blocked only
by this policy become consumable again once re-evaluated.

post.summary: Toggle a policy on or off
post.description:
Flips `is_enabled`. Returns the policy and the re-evaluation that was queued, as `PATCH`
does.

post.summary: Toggle a policy between advisory and enforcing
post.description:
Flips `is_enforcing` — the difference between a verdict that reports and one that refuses a
download, a provider serve or an apply. The highest-consequence switch on a policy, which
is why it is its own operation rather than a field on a general update.

put.summary: Override one policy for one artefact identity
put.description:
Per-instance control: inherit the org baseline, or pin this artefact's `disabled` /
`enforcing` independently of it. `inherit: true` clears the override and restores the
baseline.

inherit.description: `true` clears the override and restores the org baseline.

post.summary: Force every instance of a policy back to one enforcement level
post.description:
Clears per-instance divergence by setting every instance of this policy to `advisory` or
`enforcing`. The way out of a long tail of hand-made exceptions.

get.description:
The provider catalog: every artefact the org manages, with serve mode, constraint,
resolved source repository, blast radius (which workspaces lock it, which modules declare
it), rolling download windows, cached repository-health stats, and build/patch counts.

Every enrichment is **fault-isolated**. A failing usage, references, downloads, source-URL
or VCS-stats query degrades that column to zero or `null` for the affected rows — it never
takes the list down. So a zero here can mean "none" or "the enrichment was unavailable",
and the list is not the place to assert an absence from.

`patched_count` is a remediation claim and is therefore tier-gated: it reads `0` below the
tier that includes patched builds, even where builds exist.

post.summary: Add a provider to the catalog
post.description:
Adds a provider by hand, populates its version list from upstream, and enqueues the first
scans inline — one call, one managed provider.

`upstream` is **required**: it is part of the artefact's identity and there is no safe
default for an org that may hold both registries. An omitted `version_constraint` means
every version.

Open to every tier, because curating a provider set is not a paid capability. Whether the
org's registry *serves* it is: below that tier the row lands in `serve_mode: off` —
configuration kept, nothing advertised — rather than failing the add.

`409` only if this org already holds the row for **this** registry; the same provider from
the other registry is a separate artefact. Changing an existing row is `PATCH`.

version_constraint.description: Terraform constraint expression. Omitted or empty means all versions.

409.description: The org already manages this provider from this registry.

get.summary: Get a managed provider and its versions
get.description:
Artefact detail plus every version, each annotated with `servable` — the authorization
contract in one boolean: the bytes exist, the version satisfies the org's constraint, and
the org is entitled to it.

A version is only listed once it has a **completed scan**. An unverified version is not
hidden by accident: it is excluded on purpose, and an in-flight build appears under
`GET /api/orgs/{orgId}/provider-flows` as pipeline state instead. That keeps "a version you
can consume" and "work in progress" from ever being the same list.

`downloads.series_90d` is server-capped to the top six versions plus an `other` bucket.
`vcs_stats` is served from cache and is never a live call on this path; `null` means no
resolvable repository or a cache row the scheduled refresh has not filled yet.

patch.summary: Update a provider's constraint or serve mode
patch.description:
Partial update — an omitted field keeps its current value.

**`upstream` in the body is rejected with `400`.** The registry is the artefact's identity;
to serve the same provider from the other registry, add it again from there.

A constraint that genuinely differs from the stored value re-enqueues a scan, because a new
constraint can resolve to versions never scanned. A `serve_mode`-only change never scans,
and never touches `version_constraint`.

`serve_mode: serve` is tier-gated and answers `402` below that tier; `off` and `block` are
open to every tier.

schema.description: At least one field must be present.

400.description:
No fields to update, an invalid `serve_mode`, an unparseable `version_constraint`, or
`upstream` present in the body.

delete.summary: Remove a provider from the catalog
delete.description:
Disassociates the provider from this org. Scan results are **not** deleted — they live in a
cross-org cache keyed by provider version, so other orgs keep theirs and re-adding does not
re-scan from scratch.

The org's registry stops answering for it immediately. May refuse when something still
depends on the row.

409.description: Something still depends on this artefact.

post.description:
Enqueues a scan. With no body, the artefact's matching versions; with `version`, just that
one — and if that version names a published patched revision, its patched tree is what gets
scanned.

`200` with `status: "inflight"` means a scan for this provider is already running and
nothing new was queued. That is a success, not a conflict: the work the caller wanted is
already happening.

version.description: Scan only this version. Omit for every matching version.

200.description: A scan is already in progress; nothing new was queued.

example.message: A scan for this provider is already in progress

404.description: No such provider, or no published patched revision for the named version.

post.description:
Forces a live fetch of stars, commit activity and latest release from the source
repository, updating the cache the read paths use. Normally a scheduled job; this is the
manual nudge.

200.description: Refreshed. The body reports what was fetched or why it was skipped.

get.summary: Get a download URL for a version's SBOM
get.description:
Returns a short-lived presigned URL rather than the bytes — an SBOM is multi-megabyte SPDX
and the Worker never buffers it.

Authorization happens **before** the URL is minted: the org must manage this
`namespace/type`, the same reader gate the detail read uses. `503` means object-storage
credentials are unconfigured, which is an operator problem rather than a client one.

404.description: No such provider, or no SBOM for this version.

get.summary: Compare an upstream version with its patched revision
get.description:
The finding-level diff between the upstream base version and the newest published patched
revision: what the patch **fixed**, what **remains**, and anything it **introduced** —
plus the major-version bumps that were report-only, and the provenance of the patch (fork
repository, tag, both commit SHAs, the diff URL, any toolchain bump).

That provenance is the point: a patched binary is only trustworthy if you can see exactly
which commits produced it.

Fetched on demand when the comparison panel is expanded, so the detail payload stays light.
Tier-gated. `404` when the base version has no published patched revision, or has not been
verified yet — there is nothing honest to compare against.

403.description: The org's tier does not include patched providers.

404.description: No patched revision, or the base version is not verified yet.

get.summary: Get copy-paste instructions for consuming this provider
get.description:
The `required_providers` block pointing at this org's registry, the registry endpoint, and
the ordered commands to run — including `tofu providers lock -platform=…`, which matters
because a lock file generated on one platform fails verification on a CI runner using
another.

`servable` says whether following these instructions will actually work right now, so the
UI can warn instead of handing out instructions that will fail.

put.description:
A human decision over the policy gate for one provider version. Same precedence as
elsewhere: `block` always wins, `allow` skips the policy check, `null` restores policy
control.

post.summary: Build a provider version from source
post.description:
Compiles, gates, hashes, signs and publishes this provider version from its own source
tree, producing an artifact whose provenance Terramantle can attest to rather than a
mirrored upstream binary.

Pass the **upstream base version** (`6.3.3`), never a revision (`6.3.3-0.0.1`) — `400`
otherwise. Every self-built artifact publishes at a fresh revision `<base>-0.0.<rev>`, so a
rebuild never overwrites a previous one's bytes.

The outcome is in the body, and the distinctions matter:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `201` `status: pending` | A new build was queued. `rev` is the revision it will publish at. |
| `200` `deduped, attached: true` | An equivalent build is already running; the caller is attached to it. |
| `200` `status: entitled, deduped` | A matching build already exists and this org is now entitled to it — no rebuild. |
| `200` `status: fleet_saturated` | The build fleet is at its dispatch ceiling. Nothing was queued; retry later. |

`422` `source_unresolvable` means the provider's source repository could not be resolved to
a host that can be cloned — not a transient failure.

200.description: Deduplicated, attached, already entitled, or the fleet is saturated.

400.description: A revision was passed instead of a base version, or an unknown upstream.

409.description: A concurrent build claimed this revision. Retry.

422.description: The source repository could not be resolved to a buildable host.

post.summary: Build a CVE-remediated revision of a provider version
post.description:
Applies the scanner's dependency fixes to the upstream release tag in a private fork, then
builds and publishes the result as a new revision. Same-major bumps only — a major bump is
reported and never applied, because it can change provider behaviour.

Pass the upstream base version, not a revision. The patch is always applied **fresh from
the upstream tag**, never on top of a previous patched tree, so revisions never compound.

The statuses are the interesting part — most calls do not start a build, and each reason is
distinct:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `queued` | A patched build was dispatched. |
| `already_active` / `already_published` | A patched revision for this base is already live. |
| `nothing_to_patch` | The scan found no same-major fixable dependency CVEs. |
| `cooling_down` | A recent attempt failed; the base is in its cooldown window. |
| `abandoned` | Repeated failures; this base is no longer attempted automatically. |
| `unbuildable_base` | The base cannot be built; `failure_reason` says why. |
| `fleet_saturated` | The build fleet is at its ceiling. |

`422` covers an upstream that builds are not supported for, and a source repository that
could not be resolved to a fork.

200.description: A terminal or no-op outcome — read `status`.

400.description: A revision was passed instead of a base version, or an unknown upstream.

422.description: Unsupported upstream, or the source repository could not be resolved to a fork.

post.description:
Stops serving a published self-built artifact. `yanked_rows` is how many revision rows were
affected. The org must be entitled to the provider.

403.description: The org is not entitled to this provider.

post.summary: Clear a policy block on a provider version
post.description:
The provider counterpart of the state policy attestation: an admin reviews the findings and
accepts the risk, clearing the block so the version can be served again. A reason is
mandatory (500 characters) and `cleared_rows` is how many verdict rows were cleared.

403.description: The org is not entitled to this provider.

post.summary: Blocklist a provider version for this org
post.description:
Refuses this version for the org regardless of policy or serve mode. Blocked versions are
removed from the version list the registry advertises, so a client never resolves one.

403.description: The org is not entitled to this provider.

get.summary: Get the live build flow for a provider version
get.description:
Pipeline state for the most recent build of this version: the step timeline, the current
phase and any failure.

For an **in-flight** build the Worker queries the workflow engine live. For a finished one
it serves the stored snapshot, and `?detail=1` additionally reaches into the workflow
archive so a completed build's full timeline survives the engine's retention window.

If the engine cannot be reached the flow renders as `unknown` — deliberately never
`queued`, because "we cannot see it" and "it is waiting" are different facts and
conflating them has misled operators before.

`job_id: null` means no build has ever been attempted for this version.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: `1` also reads the workflow archive for a finished build.

post.description:
Approves one specific finding on one build gate so the build can proceed.

The approval is bound to a `finding_hash`, not to the gate as a whole: approving "this
exact finding" cannot be reused to wave through a different one that appears later. Some
gates require more than one distinct approver — the response reports `approvers`,
`required` and whether the threshold is `satisfied`, so a caller knows whether the build is
actually unblocked.

`409` once the job has reached a terminal state: overrides are not accepted retroactively.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: `provider_build_jobs.id`.

finding_hash.description: SHA-256 of the specific finding being approved.

200.description: Recorded. `satisfied: false` means more distinct approvers are still needed.

404.description: No such build job, or no user record for the caller.

409.description: The job is in a terminal state; overrides are no longer accepted.

get.summary: List the org's builds in progress
get.description:
The "builds in progress" panel: up to 50 of the org's in-flight builds, newest first, plus
any that finished in the last 15 minutes so a row shows its outcome instead of silently
vanishing mid-watch.

**Snapshot only** — this path never calls the workflow engine, however stale that makes it
(the pipeline pushes updates on a short tick). Live detail comes from the per-version
`/flow` route. Keeping a list path off the engine is what stops a slow or unreachable
cluster from hanging the Providers page.

Deliberately separate from the versions list: an unverified version is not a version yet,
and belongs here as pipeline state rather than there as something consumable.

Tombstone. The mirror/foundry split collapsed into one provider surface, and this prefix
answers `410` on **every method** while logging the caller, so a stale client shows up in
the logs of the first release after the move. A bare `404` would have been invisible.
As `/provider-mirror`, for the former foundry prefix. `410` on every method.

post.description:
The contact, founding-member and enterprise-quote forms on the marketing site. No session
exists, so **every field is visitor-supplied and untrusted**.

The gate is size caps and a tier allowlist, and the handler does exactly two things: writes
one row and emails the admin inbox. Oversized input is **rejected, not truncated**, so the
stored submission is always exactly what was sent.

A `metadata` object — the enterprise quote form's structured answers — is stored as JSON in
place of free-text `use_case`.

422.description:
A missing `name` or usable `email`, a `tier` outside the allowlist, or a field over its
cap (300 characters; 5000 for `use_case`).

post.description:
Support requests and beta feedback from inside the product.

**Name and email come from the session, not the body** — a client cannot spoof who the
feedback is from. The email is the trusted one on the user record; the name comes from the
OIDC claim. Only `company`, `tier`, `use_case` and `metadata` are read from the request.

Machine identities are refused: feedback needs a human to follow up with.

schema.description: Identity fields in the body are ignored.

metadata.description: Structured answers. Stored as JSON in place of `use_case`.

403.description: A machine identity.

422.description: The session carries no usable email, or `tier` is outside the allowlist.

post.description:
Adds the caller to the shared demo org as a `reader`, creating it on first use. Idempotent
— an existing member gets `already_member: true` rather than an error.

Seats are not counted against any quota: the demo org has unlimited readers by design.
Human only.

already_member.description: Present and `true` when the caller was already a member.

403.description: A machine identity.

404.description: The caller has no user record yet.

post.summary: Register interest in an unreleased feature
post.description:
Records that this user wants a feature that is not built yet — the "coming soon" beacon.

Always answers `200` with `status: "coming_soon"`, whatever happened underneath. That is
deliberate: the caller is a UI dialog that should never show an error for a demand signal,
and an unregistered user or a failed write is not the user's problem.

Deduplicated per user per feature by a unique constraint, so repeat clicks record once.
Any slug is accepted, but only a known shortlist notifies the team — unbounded slugs must
not amplify into an inbox.

parameters.name: feature
parameters.description: Feature slug.

403.description: A machine identity.

post.description:
Finalises a pending module version once its archive is confirmed in object storage.

Idempotent and verified at both ends: it only acts on a version still `pending`, and it
confirms the object really exists before marking it `published` — so a replayed or forged
event cannot publish bytes that are not there.

Accepts both payload shapes R2 emits: a direct single event, and an S3-compatible
`Records` array. Authenticated by a shared secret compared in constant time; a wrong or
missing secret is `403`.

`processed: 0` with `ok: true` means nothing matched — not a failure.

403.description: Missing or wrong `X-Webhook-Secret`.

post.description:
Subscription lifecycle events from Stripe. No OIDC auth — the `Stripe-Signature` header is
verified against the raw body in the handler, which is why the body must be read as text
and not re-serialised.

A rejected signature is `400`, which is what Stripe retries on.

requestBody.description: The raw Stripe event. Signature verification is over these exact bytes.

example.message: No signatures found matching the expected signature for payload

get.description:
Full-text search across module namespace, name and description. One hit is one **module**
— its latest published version plus module-level rollups — not one version.

Visibility follows the caller: anonymously, public namespaces only; authenticated, also
every org the caller belongs to (and, for a machine client, the orgs its token covers).
An additive superset of the registry search protocol: `id` keeps the protocol's
`namespace/name/provider/version` form, and the extra fields are the severity rollups the
portal's result list renders.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. Truncated to 200 characters — it becomes `LIKE` patterns.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.description: Restrict to one namespace (org slug).

get.description:
The registry protocol's version list — what `terraform init` reads to resolve a module
constraint. Published versions only, so a version still scanning is invisible to version
resolution rather than resolvable-but-unfetchable.

403.description: A private namespace the caller is not a member of.

get.description:
Everything the portal shows for one version: metadata, README, usage example, the scan
severity rollup, the findings themselves, the policy verdicts, the block state and — when
the version was published from CI over VCS trust — its source provenance.

`findings[].tool` is stripped here: which scanner found something is internal, the finding
is not.

put.description:
Streams a `.tar.gz` module archive straight to object storage and inserts a `pending`
version row, then enqueues a scan. The archive is **never** buffered in the Worker.

The version is not consumable until the scan settles: the version list and download route
only answer for `published` rows. Three ways to learn the outcome, cheapest first —

- default: `201` with `status: "pending"`, then poll `GET …/{version}/status`;
- `?wait=true`: the request long-polls up to `timeout` ms (max 15000) and returns `201`
  with the full version detail once the scan settles;
- `?wait=true` that runs out of budget: `202` with `timed_out: true`, which means the scan
  is still running, not that it failed.

Publishing from CI over VCS trust records the repository, ref and commit on the version;
a token-authenticated publish records none of that.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Module description to store alongside the version.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: `true` long-polls until the scan settles.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Long-poll budget in milliseconds. Clamped to 15000.

requestBody.description: The module archive. Streamed, not parsed.

201.description:
Published. The body is the pending acknowledgement, or — with `wait=true` and a scan
that settled in time — the full version detail.

202.description: Stored, but the scan had not settled within the `wait` budget.

409.description: This version already exists. Versions are immutable.

get.description:
The cheap poll target for a publish. Just the state machine and its timestamps — no
findings, no README — so it is safe to call in a tight CI loop.

get.summary: Resolve a module download (Registry Protocol v1)
get.description:
The registry protocol's download step: `204` with the archive URL in `X-Terraform-Get`.
There is no body.

**This is the policy gate for module consumption.** Precedence, highest first:

1. a manual block on the version — `403`;
2. a `block` serve-override on the module — `403`, even for a version with a consumable
   override;
3. an `allow` serve-override on the module, or a consumable override on the version —
   skips the policy check;
4. otherwise the version must be policy-consumable, or `403` naming the failed policies.

Refusals use the registry's `{ "errors": [...] }` envelope on purpose: `terraform` prints
`detail` verbatim, so the operator reads *why* at the point of failure.

The returned URL is a capability: either an R2 presigned URL or an HMAC-signed
`…/archive.tar.gz` on this host. Both are short-lived and need no `Authorization`, because
`terraform` does not forward one when following this header. A deprecated version also
sets `X-Terraform-Warning`.

Every resolution records a download event, with the caller's identity and Cloudflare geo
for analytics.

204.description: Resolved. The archive URL is in `X-Terraform-Get`; there is no body.

X-Terraform-Warning.description: Present only for a deprecated version — surfaced to the operator.

403.description: Blocked — manually, by a module-level serve override, or by policy.

get.description:
The bytes. Two ways in, and they are not interchangeable:

- **With `?sig=`** — the capability URL handed out by the download route. The signature is
  the authorization; no `Authorization` header is needed or read.
- **Without `sig`** — direct API access, which requires a token and org membership.

Consumability is **re-checked here**, not trusted from mint time. A URL signed before a
block was applied does not still resolve to bytes.

parameters.name: sig
parameters.description: HMAC signature from the download route. Absent means token auth is required.

403.description: Invalid or expired signature, no membership, or the version is blocked.

404.description:
No such published version, or the row points at bytes that are missing from storage —
a data-integrity signal, logged as a serve denial rather than an ordinary miss.

put.description:
Marks every version of the module deprecated. Consumption still works — deprecation warns
via `X-Terraform-Warning` rather than refusing — so this is a signal, not a block. Use the
serve override to actually stop serving.

message.description: Text surfaced to consumers. Blank or absent clears it.

delete.description: Clears module-level deprecation. Per-version deprecation is unaffected.

put.description:
The human escape hatch over the policy gate, at module scope. `block` refuses every
version including ones with their own consumable override; `allow` skips the policy check
but never a manual version block; `null` hands control back to policy.

Recorded with the acting user and the reason — this is an auditable decision to override a
machine verdict.

post.summary: Re-scan every version of a module
post.description:
Enqueues a scan for each published version. Use after a policy change that should be
re-evaluated against existing artefacts.
Enqueues a fresh scan of this version's stored archive.

post.summary: Override a policy block on one version
post.description:
Marks a version consumable despite a failing enforcing policy. `owner` only, and a reason
is mandatory — the record of who accepted the risk is the point of the endpoint.

Refuses this version outright, ahead of every other check. A reason is mandatory and is
returned to consumers in the refusal `detail`, so it should read as an instruction.

delete.description:
Clears the manual block. `owner` only — the same authority that can override a policy
verdict.

post.summary: Lift a manual block (owner, POST form)
post.description:
Identical to `DELETE …/block`. Kept because a `DELETE` with a body is awkward for some
clients. Idempotent: unblocking an unblocked version succeeds.

put.description: Same semantics as the module-level override, scoped to one version.

get.description:
The module's direct dependencies as a node/edge graph. Dependencies outside the caller's
visibility appear as stub nodes — the edge is real and worth showing even when the target
is not readable.

The portal's module list for one org. Unlike `/v1/modules/search` this is scoped to a
single namespace and requires membership, so it also shows unpublished and failed
versions — what an owner needs to see, not what a consumer may resolve.

Every version including `pending`, `processing` and `failed` — the management counterpart
of the registry protocol's published-only list.

delete.summary: Delete a module and all its versions
delete.description:
Removes the module, every version row and every stored archive. Not reversible — consumers
pinning any of those versions will fail `init` from the next run.

get.description:
The provider registry protocol's version list for one org, filtered by what that org
actually serves.

The checks run in this order, and the order is the design:

1. `serve_mode: block` ⇒ **`404`**, not `403`. A blocked provider must not advertise that
   it exists for this org.
2. no serve rule (including `serve_mode: off`) ⇒ `403` naming the provider, which is the
   actionable answer — a silent fallback to a public registry list would hand a multi-org
   user versions from an org they did not mean and fail later with a misleading
   credentials error.
3. otherwise the upstream list, narrowed to the org's version constraint and with blocked
   versions removed.

The client's `User-Agent` picks the lineage when the org manages both registries
(`OpenTofu/…` ⇒ `opentofu.org`).

403.description: Not served by this org, or the caller is not a member.

example.message: Provider hashicorp/aws is not on the allowlist for this organisation

404.description: Deliberately blocked for this org (`serve_mode: block`).

502.description:
The upstream registry could not be reached or returned something unusable. A list has
no single version to be `404` about, so every serve error here is a `502`.

get.description:
The provider registry protocol's per-platform download document: where the zip is, its
`SHA256SUMS`, the detached signature, and the GPG public key to verify it with. The three
URLs are HMAC-signed capabilities, because `tofu` does not send `Authorization` when
fetching them.

If the org serves this provider but has not mirrored this version yet, it is **pulled
through** from upstream on this request and cached — a cold download is slower, not a
failure. A genuinely new cache fill also updates the provider catalog and enqueues a scan,
off the serve path.

**Patched substitution.** `tofu` drops prereleases from range constraints client-side, so a
Terramantle-patched revision (`<base>-0.0.<rev>`) can never be chosen by a range. When
substitution is enabled, a request for the base version is answered with the latest
published, scanned, platform-complete patched revision's payload instead. Every reason
substitution does *not* happen falls through to the upstream mirror — it can only ever swap
bytes the org was already entitled to pull, never refuse.

403.description: Not served by this org, or the caller is not a member.

404.description:
No such version or platform upstream, or the provider is blocked for this org, or a
per-version block applies.

get.description:
The checksum manifest for a mirrored provider version. `upstream` selects the lineage; the
`self_built` sentinel is **not** valid here (it `404`s) because a self-built artifact needs
its lineage segment — use the `self_built/{lineage}` form below.
The detached GPG signature over `SHA256SUMS`.

get.summary: Download a provider zip (org-scoped, mirrored lineage)
get.description:
The provider binary archive. Blocks and yanks are re-checked at serve time, so a URL minted
before a block does not still resolve to bytes.

As above, for an artifact Terramantle compiled and signed itself. `lineage` is the registry
the source tree came from, and it is part of the object key — the same provider built from
both registries yields two independent artifacts.
Signed with the platform GPG key advertised in the download document.

As the org-scoped list, except the org is resolved from the token and the request host.
Prefer `/v1/providers/{orgSlug}/…`: for a user in several orgs this form is ambiguous, and
the ambiguity surfaces later as a confusing `tofu` credentials error rather than here.

If the resolved org has no serve rule for this provider the response is an actionable
`403` naming that org — deliberately not a fallback to the public registry's list.

403.description: Not served by the resolved org.

404.description: Deliberately blocked for the resolved org.

get.summary: Get the provider download document (token-scoped, legacy)
get.description:
As the org-scoped download, with the org resolved from the token and host. A token that
resolves to no org gets `403` — there is no anonymous provider serve.

403.description: The token resolves to no org, or that org does not serve this provider.

example.message: Cannot resolve organisation from token

get.description:
Accepts **either** a signed capability URL (`?sig=`) or a bearer token. With a signature
there is no user and no org: entitlement was settled when the URL was minted, and the
blocklist and yank checks still run here.

403.description: Invalid or expired signature, or no entitlement.

get.summary: Download a provider zip (token-scoped, mirrored lineage)

get.description:
What `terraform`/`tofu` fetch at the start of a run. `204` with no body means the workspace
has no state yet, which is the correct answer for a first apply rather than a `404`.

A `GET` on `.../lock` is **not** this route — lock info is deliberately not exposed on the
protocol router and answers `404`. Read it from the management API instead.

schema.description: A Terraform state file, returned verbatim.

204.description: No state stored for this workspace yet.

403.description: The token holds no read permission on this workspace.

404.description: No such org, or a `.../lock` path (not served here).

post.description:
Stores a new state version. The workspace is created on first push, so no provisioning step
is needed.

The Worker reads `serial`, `lineage` and the resource count out of the document, and
classifies managed resources into real-vs-internal counts. That classification is
best-effort and exception-safe: a hostile or oversized state stores `null` counts rather
than failing the push the client is blocking on.

Capped at 100 MB, checked against `Content-Length` first and the body length again.
Pushing enqueues a state scan.

400.description: Invalid JSON body, or an invalid workspace key.

403.description: The token holds no write permission on this workspace.

put.description:
Uploads a workspace's dependency lock file so Terramantle can see which provider versions
it actually pins. This is what populates the Locked Providers view and drives upstream
latest-version resolution, so provider drift is visible without reading the repo.

The path must end in `terraform.lock.hcl` or `.terraform.lock.hcl` — both normalise to the
same workspace, so a leading dot never forks one. 10 MB cap.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: `{workspace}/terraform.lock.hcl` or `{workspace}/.terraform.lock.hcl`.

parameters.name: X-Git-Repo-URL
parameters.description:
The infrastructure repository this lock file came from, recorded against the workspace
for attribution. Validated, not merely stored: the scheme must be `https`, `http` or
`ssh` and the value at most 2048 characters, and a value failing either is a `422`
rather than being silently dropped — a mis-set CI variable should be visible.

Omitting it is normal and keeps the previously recorded URL, if any.

requestBody.description:
The lock file, verbatim. The handler reads the body as text, so the content type is not
enforced — `text/plain` is the honest description, and `application/octet-stream` is
accepted because clients that stream the file as bytes send it.

schema.description: The lock file as raw bytes.

400.description: Not a lock-file path, or an invalid workspace key.

example.message: Only terraform.lock.hcl files are supported

422.description:
`X-Git-Repo-URL` was present but unusable — a scheme other than `https`/`http`/`ssh`,
unparseable as a URL, or over 2048 characters. The lock file is **not** stored: a bad
attribution header fails the upload rather than being discarded, so a mis-set CI
variable surfaces at the push instead of as a quietly missing repo link.

example.message: Invalid X-Git-Repo-URL

/state/{org}/{key}/lock.description:
Terraform's lock address. Spoken to with the **`LOCK`** and **`UNLOCK`** methods, which
OpenAPI cannot express - see `x-lock` and `x-unlock` on this path item for their full
definitions.

`GET` here is deliberately not served (`404`): lock state is read from
`GET /api/v1/{orgId}/state/{workspace}/lock`, which applies role-based field visibility to
the actor's personal data. `POST` answers `405`.

x-lock.description:
Terraform's `LOCK` method, sent to the lock address before an apply.

**This is where the policy gate stops an apply.** The gate runs *before* the lock row is
created: a workspace whose latest state violates an enforcing policy is refused `423` here,
so the apply never starts and `tofu` never mutates infrastructure. Clearing it needs a
human attestation (`POST /api/v1/{orgId}/state/{workspace}/policy/attest`) — deliberately
not something the CI token that tripped it can do for itself.

Actor metadata (IP, geo, name) is captured for display and audit only. The IP comes from
`CF-Connecting-IP` alone, never `X-Forwarded-For`, because that header is client-spoofable.

requestBody.description: Terraform's lock info. Absent or unparseable is tolerated.

403.description: The token holds no write permission on this workspace.

423.description:
The policy gate blocked this workspace. An admin must attest before the next apply can
start.

example.message: Workspace is blocked by an enforcing policy

x-unlock.description:
Terraform's `UNLOCK`. Idempotent — unlocking a workspace with no lock, or no workspace at
all, succeeds, because Terraform treats a failed unlock as a stuck lock.

The apply-run analytics row is closed off the critical path: a slow or failed analytics
write must never delay the unlock the client is waiting on.

200.description: Released, or there was nothing to release.

get.description:
Every workspace in the org with its latest version's rollup: serial, resource counts,
scan severity counts, policy compliance, current lock and who pushed last.

`tenant_id` is never projected into the response — the query selects explicit columns
rather than `*` so it cannot leak.

A connected view of what this org's infrastructure depends on: workspaces `locks`
providers (from lock files), and registry modules `requires` providers (matched on the
module's primary provider type).

A module with no matching provider node is omitted on purpose — the value is a connected
graph, not a field of orphans. A provider node is marked `outdated` when any workspace
pins an older version than the newest one matching its constraint.

delete.summary: Delete a workspace and all its state
delete.description:
Removes the workspace, every version and every stored state object. `owner` and human only,
and not reversible — the next apply against that key starts from nothing. Idempotent: a
workspace that does not exist returns `ok`.

200.description: Deleted, or there was nothing to delete.

get.description:
Version history, newest first. Each entry carries the serial, resource counts, scan
severity counts, policy compliance, the LOCK→push duration of the apply that produced it,
and — for a restore — the serial it was promoted from.

Push counts per UTC day, the slowest applies, apply-runtime statistics, and lifetime
totals.

The day series is **sparse** — days with no pushes are omitted and the client zero-fills.
`window_days` is echoed so a caption never hardcodes the window, and `totals` is lifetime
rather than windowed so "N versions" is not a lie.

Security findings from scanning the stored state: secrets, exposed endpoints and open
ports.

`tool` is omitted — which scanner found something stays internal. A finding whose stored
metadata is malformed degrades to `meta: null` rather than failing the whole list, because
the client has no retry for a `500` here.

`{ "lock": null }` when the workspace is unlocked, or does not exist.

**Field visibility depends on role.** Actor origin — IP, city, country, name and the raw
lock info blob — is personal data and is gated to `member` and above. A `reader` learns
that a lock exists and what operation holds it, but not who or where from.

delete.description:
Clears a stuck lock. `member` and above, **human only** — a bot that wedged a lock cannot
clear it for itself.

The caller must name the exact `lock_id`, following Terraform's own force-unlock model, so
a stale UI cannot clobber a lock that has since rotated. Idempotent: an already-unlocked
workspace returns `ok`.

ID.description: The lock id to release. Must match the held lock.

409.description: The supplied `lock_id` does not match the held lock.

404.description: No such workspace, or it has no versions to scan.

patch.description: Per-workspace settings, such as the infrastructure repository URL.

put.description:
A human decision that outranks the state policy gate for this workspace. Admin and human
only; recorded with the acting user and reason.

post.summary: Clear a policy block on a workspace
post.description:
The escape hatch for the LOCK-gate deadlock. A workspace whose latest state violates an
enforcing policy refuses the next apply at `LOCK`; an admin reviews the findings and
attests — either that the fix is in, or that the risk is accepted — which clears the block.

Admin and **human** only: a CI token that trips a policy cannot self-attest. That is
two-person control, matching the force-unlock and promote gates.

Two modes:

- `one_shot` (default) — re-evaluated on the next apply, and re-blocks if it still
  violates.
- `sticky` — stays cleared until something blocks it again explicitly.

A reason is mandatory (500 characters).

200.description:
Attested. `cleared: false` means the workspace was not blocked in the first place —
not a failure.

value.message: Workspace was not blocked by policy

get.description:
What the workspace's lock file pins, each row enriched with the vulnerability rollup for
**both** the version in use and the version an upgrade would land on — so the question
"is upgrading worth it" is answerable from one call.

`current_scan` / `latest_scan` are `null` where that version has no completed scan. That
is deliberately distinct from an empty rollup: `null` means *not scanned*, an empty rollup
means *scanned and clean*.

`truncated: true` means the provider list hit its row cap. `lock_file` is `null` and
`providers` empty when no lock file has been uploaded.

post.description:
Re-publishes the lock file's providers for upstream latest-version resolution, refreshing
the drift view. `queued: false` with `providers: 0` means there was nothing to resolve.

404.description: No such workspace, or no lock file uploaded.

post.description:
Copies an earlier version forward as a **new** version at the next serial, rather than
rewriting history — so the restore is itself auditable and is undone by promoting again.

Admin and human only, and guarded by `Idempotency-Key`: a retried or double-clicked
restore returns the version the first call created, with `idempotent_replay: true`, instead
of writing a second byte-identical copy at a new serial.

`source_serial` is the serial that was restored from. Can be disabled by a deploy-time
switch, in which case this returns `404`.

200.description: Restored, or a replay of an earlier identical call.

404.description: No such workspace or version, or the feature is disabled.

423.description: The workspace is locked by a running apply.

get.description:
The Resource Inspector's data: managed resources as a tree, built from the stored state.
With `compare`, the tree is diffed against another version so added, removed and changed
resources are distinguishable.

No resource **values** are returned — this is addresses and structural metadata only.

parameters.name: compare
parameters.description: Another version id to diff against.

post.description:
Removes the named resource addresses and writes the result forward as a **new** version at
the next serial — the same copy-forward model as a restore, so the removal is auditable and
undone by promoting an earlier serial.

This silently changes what the next apply plans against, for the whole workspace. It is
therefore admin + human only, requires `Idempotency-Key`, and holds a real lock for the
copy so a concurrent apply cannot interleave — if the workspace is already locked it
returns `423`.

Works against **any** version, not just the tip: the new tip becomes that version's body
minus the removed addresses. Can be disabled by a deploy-time switch, in which case this
returns `404`.

200.description: Removed, or a replay of an earlier identical call.

404.description: No such workspace or version, or the feature is disabled.

423.description: The workspace is locked by a running apply.
